title: Dev machine never installed the lock: fastapi 0.115.0/pytest 8.2.0 local vs fastapi 0.141.1/pytest 9.1.1 on CI and Railway prod
evidence: requirements.txt:47 pins fastapi==0.141.1 (locked at f85533a, PR #82, 2026-08-25; requirements.in floats fastapi>=0.109.0); requirements-dev.txt pins pytest==9.1.1. On the dev machine: `python -c "import fastapi; print(fastapi.__version__)"` -> 0.115.0, `python -m pytest --version` -> 8.2.0. CI installs the lock (Install dependencies step), Railway/Nixpacks installs requirements.txt, so CI AND PROD run a FastAPI 26 minor versions newer than anything ever exercised locally. Direct consequence: tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt (header lines 5-10) claims it was captured in 'the exact state of CI', yet its 14 rows diverge from CI's 16 in BOTH directions — it misses the 3 route-table failures (CD-ci-truth-02) and carries test_database_service::test_save_comparison_skips_when_not_renderable (line 45) which passes on CI. Every W1-W4 'branch-only-NEW == []' comm gate ran under the mismatched versions.
fix: Run `pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt` on the dev machine (ideally a project venv), then re-capture tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt under the locked versions. Make version parity a gate: have scripts/regression_gate_diff.py (or a conftest check) assert `fastapi.__version__`/`pytest.__version__` match the lock before trusting a baseline capture.
verify_reason: Independently re-derived every leg: local `python -c` prints fastapi 0.115.0 / pytest 8.2.0 vs requirements.txt:47 fastapi==0.141.1 (lock commit f85533a verified via git show) and requirements-dev.txt:107 pytest==9.1.1; ci.yml:27 installs both locks; tests/.pre_impl_failures.txt:5-10 claims 'the exact state of CI' yet CI run 33471608741 shows 16 failures diverging from the 14-row baseline in BOTH directions (baseline misses the 3 route-table reds; baseline row test_database_service line 45 passed on CI). Prod/CI run a FastAPI never exercised by any local gate run (local 13 failed vs CI 16). Same defect class M13-17 was rated P1 for; this is the residual the recapture could not see, not a re-file.

title: Branch protection requires only the three jobs that structurally cannot fail on their signal; backend-tests (15,747 tests) is not a required check
evidence: `gh api repos/KGRddhs/smartcompare-backend/branches/main/protection` -> required contexts = [backend-lint, dependency-audit, frontend-typecheck]; backend-tests and frontend-tests absent; enforce_admins false; strict false. Of the three required: dependency-audit's ONLY substantive steps both carry continue-on-error (ci.yml:178 pip-audit, ci.yml:186 npm audit) so it can only go red on a pip install failure; frontend-typecheck's tsc step carries continue-on-error (ci.yml:205) so it can only go red on npm ci. Net effect: a PR that breaks 16 backend tests (today's main) or any number of type errors merges with all required checks green — the merge gate is decorative exactly where it matters.
fix: After the 16 reds are cleared (CD-ci-truth-02/09/10 cover all of them), add backend-tests to required status checks (the #89 acceptance criterion); independently, dropping the tsc continue-on-error (CD-ci-truth-07) makes frontend-typecheck a real check immediately since tsc is currently green.

title: W3xW3: M13-35 drain defeats M13-37 refund - pre-verdict disconnect burns a credit + full OpenAI tail
evidence: LIVE IN PROD (both fixes unflagged). On disconnect the stream sets client_gone and DRAINS (text_routes.py:561-568); when the orchestrator eventually yields `complete`, the finally takes the meter branch (:576-604: log_search success + save_comparison + record_lifetime_comparison) and the gate-consumed credit (:486-497) is never refunded - the else-refund (:622-634) requires complete_response to be absent. Pre-wave (git show 674034e:app/api/text_routes.py, generator lines ~493-496) a disconnect hit `return`: no consume existed, no metering ran - a dropped connection was free. Now a network blip at second 2 of a ~30s stream burns 1 of 3 daily + monthly + lifetime credits AND runs the full default-UNBOUNDED OpenAI tail. Verified the drain actually executes on the prod stack: pinned starlette==1.6.0 (wheel inspected: StreamingResponse.__call__ at spec_version>=2.4 has NO listen_for_disconnect task; disconnect surfaces only via send(), which the drain stops calling) + uvicorn advertises spec_version 2.4; Request.is_disconnected (requests.py:328) correctly reads the disconnect between events. So CLAUDE.md's M13-37 closeout claim that the else-refund covers 'a pre-verdict cancel' is wrong for the dominant real-disconnect path - the drain prevents the cancel; only orchestrator raises reach the else branch.
fix: In the finally, treat `client_gone and complete_response captured only after client_gone` as the refund/no-meter case (track when the payload landed vs when the client left), or gate the drain itself on complete_response already captured (the option CLAUDE.md's M13-35 note names) so a pre-verdict disconnect cancels, refunds via the else branch, and stops the OpenAI tail. Keep metering for post-verdict drops.
verify_reason: Mechanism independently re-derived and CONFIRMED: on disconnect the generator sets client_gone and drains (text_routes.py:561-568); the orchestrator's eventual `complete` is captured (:556-557) so the finally takes the meter branch (:576-604 — log_search success + save_comparison + record_lifetime_comparison) and the gate-consumed credit (:486-497) is never refunded (else-refund :622-634 requires complete_response absent). Pre-wave `git show 674034e` verified: disconnect hit `return` at old :495 and the gate was read-only check_usage_allowed — a drop was free. Version claim corroborated where checkable: requirements.txt pins starlette==1.6.0/uvicorn==0.52.4, and local uvicorn h11+httptools both advertise spec_version 2.4 (verified by inspection), so starlette's post-0.39 spec>=2.4 path (no listen_for_disconnect task; disconnect surfaces only via send(), which the drain stops calling) applies — the generator is NOT cancelled and runs to completion. Both fixes unflagged = live at 593ec1e, and CLAUDE.md's M13-37/M13-35 closeout claims are wrong for the real-disconnect path. DOWNGRADED to P2 for severity consistency with the review's own scale: the originals this interaction sits between (M13-35 metering bypass, M13-37 quota TOCTOU) were both P2 while live; the OpenAI-tail half is already a documented accepted trade-off (CLAUDE.md M13-35 resource note), and the burned credit corresponds to a comparison that IS persisted to the user's history (save_comparison runs), softening 'burns a credit for nothing'. Real, live, should gate the drain on complete_response-already-captured — but P2-class harm, not P1.

title: W2: region-currency guard covers only the final projection - SSE prices event and scores/verdict still consume the unguarded price
evidence: ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD (M13-11) pends only inside build_comparison_response (response_builder.py:1246-1267). Two consumers bypass that chokepoint: (a) the streaming `prices` event builds its own pending-normalization block (scs:3806-3835) that applies SIB-5 + is_price_showable but NOT the region guard - flag ON, a BHD price on a saudi_arabia request is streamed raw to the client, then retracted by the final `complete` payload; (b) scoring_service.compute_scores runs BEFORE the guard on BOTH paths (scs:3897 streaming, scs:3205 sync) over raw product_data, and the verdict is generated from that scoring_result - so winner_index/dimension_winners/win_margin and the LLM verdict are still decided by the mismatched amount (a BHD 10 vs SAR 40 pair scores as 10-vs-40), exactly the harm the guard's own comment cites ('a mislabelled price wins or loses the comparison'). The final payload then shows price 'pending' with a winner chosen by the hidden price; only response_builder's _build_scoring_v2 price dim is honest. A canary that checks final payloads sees pends and wrongly concludes the guard works.
fix: Apply the region-currency pend where the other pends already live in the streaming prices block (scs:3819 condition), and move/duplicate the guard to run on product_data BEFORE compute_scores (or null the amount pre-scoring the way the chokepoint comment assumes) so scores/verdict take the missing-data path. Add a streaming-path assertion to the wave's guard tests before the runbook's final-window flip.
verify_reason: Both bypass claims CONFIRMED by direct read: (a) the streaming `prices` event block (scs:3806-3835) applies SIB-5 + is_price_showable(enforce_correctness=True) but never region_currency_guard_enabled — grep confirms ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD is referenced ONLY in price_service.py:686-702 (reader) and response_builder.py:1211-1258 (chokepoint), so flag-ON a foreign-currency price streams raw mid-stream (is_price_showable takes no region param and cannot pend it); (b) compute_scores runs on raw product_data at scs:3897 (streaming) and scs:3205 (sync) BEFORE build_comparison_response applies the guard, and generate_comparison (scs:3227) consumes that scores_summary — so winner/dimension_winners/verdict are decided by the mismatched amount, which is the exact harm the guard's own comment at response_builder.py:1246-1250 cites, and a final-payload canary sees pends and passes. Not a duplicate: M13-11's row prescribed the chokepoint guard but the review could not see that the implementation leaves the row's stated failure scenario ('the 10x-wrong product wins') unfixed. DOWNGRADED to P2 by the review's own convention (M13-38 was downgraded P1->P2 for exactly this shape: default-OFF flag, harm only on activation, cost = a canary that reads clean while the real blocker goes unnamed). Zero live delta today; must be treated as a hard precondition on the runbook's region-guard flip.

The client's documented SSE→non-streaming fallback consumes a second slot from the same shared bucket, doubling pressure exactly at the ceiling. This is the FIRST breaker in any compare storm and binds ~10x below every other ceiling's flags-on potential.

title: Flags-off event-loop blocking bounds the whole service at ~0.15-0.5 cold compares/s and ~0.4-0.5 app-opens/s at the measured 163ms Upstash RTT
evidence: With ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD and ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD both OFF (Railway-verified), run_db executes Supabase .execute() inline on the loop (db_offload.py:38-40) and every Upstash command is a blocking HTTPS RTT through the shared sync REST client (cache_service.py:18-28, 53-64). Arithmetic per authed COLD compare: 40-60 Redis commands x 163ms (M13-06's own measurement) = 6.5-10s + 5-8 Supabase/GoTrue calls x 50-100ms ≈ 0.5s of SERIALIZED loop time; warm compare 3-5s; app-open (4-5 authed reqs: verify_token GoTrue RTT each at auth_service.py:254 + usage/status 2 selects + 2 GETs) ≈ 2.0-2.6s. Loop capacity = 1s/s → ceilings ≈ 0.1-0.3 concurrent cold compares/s or 0.4-0.5 app-opens/s; p95 spirals from ~60% utilization. Because the 15s price race and 30s cap are wall-clock, other tenants' loop stalls convert directly into hard-cap TIMEOUTs and adapter Nones — quality degrades before any error rate moves. Post-response fire-and-forget writes (log_search, save_comparison_and_track_cohort — explicitly OUTSIDE the M13-05 hot set) add 2-4 more blocking calls per completed compare.
fix: Two-part lever, in order of measured impact: (1) Redis RTT: move Upstash to the same region as the Railway service (163ms → single-digit ms is a 20-30x reduction in stall; the offload flags alone only relocate the 163ms from loop to the 40-thread pool ≈ 8 thread-s/compare); (2) then canary ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD and ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD per their preconditions (M13-31 atomic half-open first), and wrap log_search/save_comparison_and_track_cohort in run_db in the next wave as CLAUDE.md already schedules.
verify_reason: Structure fully code-verified: run_db executes inline flag-off (db_offload.py:38-40); one module-global sync Upstash REST client (cache_service.py:18-28) with every command a blocking HTTPS RTT on the loop; verify_token's GoTrue get_user (auth_service.py:254), tier-info and referral-bonus selects (usage_service.py:290/360) all behind run_db=inline; user-scoped Supabase client is a new create_client per call (database_service.py:48-54) vs cached admin (:38-45); log_search/save_comparison_and_track_cohort confirmed outside the M13-05 hot set (db_offload docstring + CLAUDE.md W3 deferred list). Arithmetic re-derived and consistent: 40-60×163ms=6.5-9.8s cold, 20-30×163ms=3.3-4.9s warm (the 20-30 warm count is M13-06's own row verbatim), ~2.0-2.6s per app-open, knees at ~0.4-0.5 opens/s. Not a duplicate: M13-05/06 filed the inventories; the compares/s / opens/s ceilings and the flags-ON-just-moves-the-wall-to-the-pool observation are new. One material caveat the finding should carry forward: 163ms traces to serper_service.py:214 'measured 163ms in this worktree' — a LOCAL dev-machine measurement reused by M13-06, NOT a Railway→Upstash measurement; prod RTT is unmeasured and could be several-fold lower, moving the knee accordingly (the finding does bracket the same-region case, and even at ~20-50ms datacenter RTT the blocking-on-loop structure still caps low single-digit compares/s). P1 stands.

title: OpenAI Tier-1 TPM caps the restored product at ~6-10 compares/min, and a 429 storm triples request volume with an unbounded flags-off SSE tail
evidence: Clients are built with no max_retries override → SDK default 2 retries/call, httpx.Timeout(120, connect=30). Per-compare token profile: cold ≈ 19-25k mini + 4.5k gpt-4o (verdict); warm ≈ 5.2k. At Tier 1 (500 RPM / 200K TPM mini; 500 RPM / 30K TPM 4o): mini TPM binds at 200K/20K = 10 cold compares/min; 4o verdict TPM binds at 30K/4.5K = 6.6/min. model_router's breaker (model_router_service.py:37-64) only flips on the DAILY 1M-token counter at 80% — zero TPM protection, so the first wall is hit mid-minute, not mid-day. 429-storm amplification: every call becomes 3 attempts; the verdict chain (extraction_service.py:2349-2376) runs up to 3x gpt-4o + 3x mini = 6 attempts. Phase-1 retries are cancelled by the 8s/10s wait_fors (wasted RPM, bounded), but the streaming tail with ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE OFF awaits verdict/critique/moderation directly (structured_comparison_service.py:3936-3944, 3965-3973): under slow-mode degradation a single tail call can hold the SSE connection up to ~6.5min (3x120s+backoff), worst chain ~13min, with M13-35 drain keeping abandoned streams burning server-side.
fix: Before re-funding OpenAI: (a) verify the account tier and size the launch at TPM/token-profile arithmetic (Tier 3+ or verdict-on-mini for any real traffic; a verdict-dedupe/cache for repeated pairs would also lift the 6.6/min 4o wall); (b) set an explicit max_retries=0-1 and a shorter timeout on the Phase-1-facing client so wait_for-cancelled retries stop burning RPM; (c) treat ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE=ON as a precondition for any OpenAI-degradation scenario so tails cap at the 30s residual.
verify_reason: Code claims verified: openai_service.py:27 builds AsyncOpenAI with httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=30.0) and NO max_retries override (SDK default 2 → 3 attempts/call); the verdict chain retries once onto the standard model on 429 (extraction_service.py:2349-2376) → worst 3×4o + 3×mini = 6 attempts; model_router's breaker reads only the DAILY 1M counter at 80% (model_router_service.py:37,41,46-64) — zero TPM awareness; flag-off tail awaits verdict and critique directly (scs:3936-3944, 3965-3973), matching M13-04-OFF. Arithmetic re-derived: 30K TPM/4.5K = 6.6 verdicts/min, 200K/20K = 10 cold/min — correct against OpenAI's published Tier-1 limits (gpt-4o 30K TPM, gpt-4o-mini 200K TPM); ~6.5min single-call worst (3×120s+backoff) and ~13min chain worst follow. The Tier-1 premise is an explicit unverified assumption (account tier unknown, currently 429ing on no credits) and the finding's own fix item is to verify it — conditional framing, not speculation-as-measurement. Not a duplicate: M13-04 filed the unbounded tail; the TPM arithmetic, daily-counter TPM blind spot, and x3-x6 retry amplification are new. P1 appropriate as a launch-sizing gate for the restored product.

title: /home/savings does an UNBOUNDED all-rows full_response SELECT synchronously on the event loop
evidence: home_savings (home_routes.py:138-158) on a 5-min cache miss runs client.table('comparisons').select('full_response').eq('user_id',...).eq('schema_version',2).execute() with NO .limit() and NO column projection beyond the single largest column, inside async def, sync client. full_response is the complete comparison payload (~50-200KB/row). A user with 100 comparisons pulls 5-20MB through a blocking socket read: 1-5s+ of loop stall, growing linearly with history forever. It fires on app-open (SavingsBanner) and only needs SUM/COUNT of two floats per row. Not in the M13-05 run_db hot set and not touched by ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD — it stays inline even with every W3 flag ON. The 5-min TTL means every active user re-pays it 12x/hour.
fix: Compute the aggregate in SQL (an RPC or a generated column / view summing winner-loser deltas server-side), or at minimum select only the two price fields via a jsonb path and add a hard .limit(). Wrap whatever remains in run_db and lengthen the cache TTL (savings changes only on new comparisons - bust on save instead of 5-min expiry).
verify_reason: Every element verified at file:line. home_routes.py:152-158 selects only 'full_response' with NO .limit() and no projection, via a sync supabase execute inside async def; the aggregate loop at :165-174 needs exactly two floats per row; _SAVINGS_TTL_SECONDS = 5*60 at :53 so each active user re-pays it 12x/hour. It is in neither ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD's hot set (CLAUDE.md W3 enumerates 9 sites, none in home_routes) nor the Redis-offload dispatch (savings uses _redis_get/_redis_set directly, home_routes.py:138/183), so it stays inline with all flags ON. M13 overlap claim verified: grep of docs/investigations/2026-08-31-m13-full-review.md for home_routes|home_savings|smart_pick|/home/ returns zero rows. Linear-forever growth on an app-open endpoint on a 1-loop deployment justifies P1; the 1-5s figure is an estimate from declared RTT/payload inputs, labeled as such.

Simultaneously, the 21 undecorated routes have NO limit at all because SlowAPIMiddleware is not registered (ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS off).

title: Flags-off event loop: inline sync Supabase+Upstash caps compare throughput at ~0.5-2.5/s and converts concurrency into 30s-cap timeouts

title: All decorated per-route limits share ONE deployment-wide bucket (key = shared Railway edge-proxy IP) — global capacity ceiling and near-free per-route DoS lever
evidence: With ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT OFF (prod default; var is unset in Railway), _rate_limit_key returns get_remote_address(request)=request.client.host (rate_limiter.py:52-59), and the Limiter is built with that key_func (rate_limiter.py:125-129). No --proxy-headers/--forwarded-allow-ips exists in Procfile/railway.json (both start commands are bare 'uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT'), and uvicorn's default forwarded-allow-ips=127.0.0.1 excludes the Railway proxy peer (100.0.0.0/8 per Railway edge-networking docs), so request.client.host is the shared internal edge-proxy IP for EVERY caller. slowapi keys each decorated bucket on (key_func result, route scope), so all users hitting one route collapse into ONE bucket. Decorated limits enforce today regardless of the SlowAPIMiddleware gate. Effective deployment-wide TOTAL ceilings: POST /text/compare 10/min (text_routes.py:133), POST /auth/register 3/min (auth_routes.py:330), POST /auth/login 5/min (auth_routes.py:451), DELETE /auth/account 1/min (auth_routes.py:735). Add a test asserting two requests with different client IPs get different limiter keys.

title: SSE streaming is dead on-device: every text compare silently runs TWO full backend comparisons back-to-back with zero progress UI
evidence: streamComparison uses global fetch + response.body.getReader() (api.ts:410-419). React Native 0.81.5's fetch is the whatwg-fetch polyfill (node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Network/fetch.js:15 `require('whatwg-fetch')`) and `grep -c ReadableStream node_modules/whatwg-fetch/dist/fetch.umd.js` = 0 — Response has no .body stream, and whatwg-fetch resolves only on XHR onload (full body buffered). Expo's winter runtime installs TextDecoder but never replaces global fetch (node_modules/expo/src/winter/runtime.native.ts — 'ReadableStream is injected by Metro as a global' comment; streaming fetch is opt-in via `expo/fetch`, not imported anywhere in src/). Therefore on every device call: (1) the fetch to /text/compare/stream buffers the ENTIRE SSE stream — the backend runs a full comparison and the client discards every status/specs/prices event unparsed; (2) `!response.body` at api.ts:415 throws 'Stream failed: 200'; (3) the catch (api.ts:482-535) issues a SECOND compare via axios GET /text/compare. Net: serial double workload per tap, wall time ≈ full compare + re-serve, statusMessage in HomeScreen never advances past 'finding', and the L3.7 wallTime tracker marks ttfb at completion (HomeScreen.tsx:315-321 onStatus/onComplete) — the '88s wall-time gap' instrumentation (HomeScreen.tsx:75-80) is measuring this defect. Backend M13-35 drain-not-abandon makes the abandoned-stream cost a guaranteed full server-side compare. Jest passes because tests mock fetch with a body. Verify on-device with one log: `console.log(typeof response.body)` → undefined.
fix: Import the streaming-capable fetch from 'expo/fetch' inside streamComparison (SDK 54 supports it; JS-only change, OTA-able via eas update) so response.body is a real ReadableStream; keep the whatwg fallback for exotic failures but log a Sentry breadcrumb when it engages so a silent regression is visible. Until then, skip the stream attempt entirely and call GET /text/compare once — one compare instead of two.
verify_reason: Independently re-derived: grep shows abortRef's only sites are declaration (HomeScreen.tsx:112), assignment (:313), and nulling (:324, :352) — never called; the sole unmount cleanup (:187-194) clears only advanceTimerRef; the fullscreen loader (:856-865) is pointerEvents="auto" with no cancel affordance; streamComparison returns abort (api.ts:539) and the axios fallback GET (:509-512) rides the same never-aborted controller. title: Trust rules + category personalities mandate quantified (and compliance) claims the data cannot support, and no downstream layer verifies verdict prose numbers
evidence: UNIVERSAL_TRUST_RULES (prompt_personalities.py:72) - injected into EVERY verdict via build_personality_prompt (:94) - orders: 'NO vague language: "somewhat better" is NEVER acceptable - quantify or explain specifically', directly contradicting COMPARISON_SYSTEM's own softer rule (extraction_service.py:982 'INCLUDE a specific number... when available; otherwise use a concrete qualitative attribute'). The personality evidence_language blocks then model precise figures as the required style: electronics :6 ('Product A delivers 23% better battery life (14h vs 11.4h) - never "somewhat better"'), makeup :27 ('12-hour wear without oxidation', '40 shades'), fragrances :48 (invent a note pyramid in evocative detail). Grocery risk_framing :14 instructs 'In GCC: halal compliance' - but no grocery schema field carries halal certification (extraction_service.py:114-118), so any halal-compliance statement is fabricated; a wrong halal claim is a top-tier harm in this market. The verdict's input specs are largely 'N/A'-stamped or training-sourced with the no-fab flag OFF, yet NOTHING checks prose numbers: trust_validation_service.py:46-129 compares only dimension scores/winner index, fact_check_service.verify_spec_citations:18-70 checks only spec-field citations, and text_sanitize.strip_score_internals removes only internal-score phrasing. A '23%'/'14h vs 11.4h' style claim invented to satisfy the trust rules ships unchecked, is persisted, and is re-served from Home/History/Share.
fix: Rewrite the trust rule to be evidence-conditional: 'quantify ONLY with a number present in the supplied product data; when the data has no number, a qualitative comparison is correct - never invent precision'. title: CATEGORY_MIN_COVERAGE penalty is inverted in effect - a 1-field product outscores a full-spec product 3.9x

title: Migration 013 cohort views over users PII have no security_invoker and no REVOKE — RLS-bypassing read of aggregate demographics

title: Push crons have no overlap protection: send-then-stamp with no atomic claim double-pushes on concurrent runs and permanently drops reminders on failed sends
evidence: cron_expire_bonuses.py:155-157 loops `await _send_reminder(row)` then `await _mark_reminder_sent(...)`. _send_reminder (lines 130-134) swallows every exception, and _mark_reminder_sent stamps unconditionally — so an Expo outage during a run permanently consumes every reminder (stamped sent, filter at line 78 `.is_("expiry_reminder_sent_at","null")` excludes them forever) with no retry. Conversely, two overlapping instances (Railway retry, manual run beside the scheduled one — the docstrings say "safe to retry") both fetch the same NULL-stamped rows and both push before either stamps. Same shape in cron_reengagement.py:150-151: the 7-day cap is a read-then-insert (reengagement_service.py:132-149 counts re_engagement_events, cron inserts at _record_event then dispatches) with no conditional claim; grep for setnx/lock/lease across scripts/cron_*.py returns nothing — no cron takes a run-level mutex.
fix: Take a per-run Redis lease (SET cron:<name>:lock NX EX <ttl>) at main() entry, and make the stamp a conditional claim: UPDATE ... SET expiry_reminder_sent_at=now() WHERE id=? AND expiry_reminder_sent_at IS NULL executed BEFORE the send, sending only when the update reports a row changed (flips to at-most-once with an atomic claim; the failed-send case then needs a separate 'send failed' unstamp or a delivered_at column if at-least-once is wanted).
verify_reason: Independently re-derived: cron_expire_bonuses.py:156-157 sends then stamps; _send_reminder (119-134) swallows every exception and _mark_reminder_sent (88-97) stamps unconditionally, so an Expo outage permanently consumes reminders (fetch filter .is_('expiry_reminder_sent_at','null') at line 78 excludes them forever) while docstrings (123, 138) claim 'safe to retry'. M13 touched these crons only for sys.path (M13-107) and coverage floor (M13-77) — not a duplicate. title: Arabic-locale Contact Us breaks the documented `[Bug]%` grep contract — the prefix is the LOCALIZED category label

title: Admin analytics endpoints run unbounded full-table scans + N+1 sequential BLOCKING Supabase calls on the event loop
evidence: Three admin GETs issue synchronous `.execute()` (blocking HTTP round-trips) inside async handlers with no bound tied to table size: (1) cohort_metrics line 297 `client.table("users").select("preferences").execute()` — whole users table, no .limit(); (2) cohort_retention lines 362-377 — all users since cutoff, then ONE user_events query PER USER inside the loop; (3) referrals_cohort_uplift lines 573-607 — all redemptions + all users, then `_stats_for` fires one count query per user for up to 500+500 users. title: M13-31 rewrite can lock a provider breaker in HALF_OPEN indefinitely: every gate check consumes the probe AND refreshes the 1h state TTL, but nothing guarantees the probe ever records
evidence: UNFLAGGED, live now. api_budget_service.py:514-522: in HALF_OPEN every is_circuit_closed() call does half_open_calls += 1 then _redis_set(..., ex=_CB_TTL) (TTL 3600, line 270) and returns half_open_calls <= CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS (=1, line 255). Two routine paths spend the single probe slot without ever producing a record_success/record_failure: (a) the composed gate `is_circuit_closed(p) and has_budget(p)` (structured_comparison_service.py:884, brightdata_service.py:79) — the breaker check passes (probe consumed) then has_budget() fails, so no provider call fires; (b) the 15s price race cancels a pending _firecrawl_scraper/_scrapedo_scraper coroutine mid-HTTP (routine loser-cancellation), so the service-level record_* is skipped. Once the probe is spent, every later check returns False AND re-SETs the state with a fresh 1h TTL — under steady compare traffic the HALF_OPEN state never expires and nothing can ever record (no calls are admitted), so the provider is locked out permanently, not for the 10-min CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT. Pre-wave behaviour (admit everything in half-open) was leaky but self-healing: the first completed call closed or re-tripped the breaker. record_success (line 553-565) / record_failure (line 529-548) are the only exits and both require an admitted, completed call.
fix: Do not refresh the TTL on a read-side check (compute remaining TTL, or store tripped_at and derive expiry), and/or re-arm the probe when another CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT has elapsed since the last admission (store half_open_admitted_at and reset half_open_calls when stale). Alternatively count the probe at the call site (after has_budget and before dispatch) instead of inside the status check.
verify_reason: Mechanism independently re-derived and it is real. api_budget_service.py:513-522 (post-c8531b4): the HALF_OPEN branch does half_open_calls += 1 then _redis_set(key, ..., ex=_CB_TTL) on EVERY read-side check, so any check refreshes the 1h TTL; CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS=1 (line 255) means the first check spends the only probe; record_success/record_failure are the only exits and both require an admitted, completed call. I also found a probe-consuming path STRONGER than the two filed: scs.py:1423 passes the gate, then at :1448-1455 an empty-html response with status 403/404 records NEITHER failure (only 429/503/0) NOR success, so the probe is spent with no state transition. Claim (a) is real too — scs:882/884 evaluates is_circuit_closed BEFORE has_budget, so a budget-out short-circuits after the probe is burned. Not a re-file of M13-31 (docs/investigations/2026-08-31-m13-full-review.md:60 is the never-incremented counter, now fixed); this is a new mode the fix created. DOWNGRADED to P2 because (i) 'permanent' holds only while some caller checks that provider at least once per 3600s — at today's pre-activation traffic the key simply expires and self-heals; (ii) the failure direction is conservative (a paid render provider is skipped, no wrong price, no money moved); (iii) the repo's own scale put M13-31, M13-35 and the freemium TOCTOU M13-37 at P2, and this is the same class.

title: Streaming route still burns the freemium credit on cold-path timeouts: STREAM_TIMEOUT / INSUFFICIENT_DATA terminals arrive as settle_complete/complete with success:false, so the M13-35 finally meters them as SUCCESS (no refund, lifetime++, log_search success=True)

title: M13-10 stash parity is broken against M13-09: the short-circuit seed does not apply the strict-shopping currency pend, so with ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY ON the fairness re-select can serve the exact mislabelled price the flag pends
evidence: Main path (price_service.py:9459-9474): with the flag ON, a letter-dollar item ('R$ 1.399' — detect_currency says USD) and an unresolved foreign-glyph item ('1,399 د.إ' on a BHD ask — detect_currency None) are skipped via `continue`. Stash path (_seed_shortcircuit_candidates, structured_comparison_service.py:7397-7439, rewritten this wave for M13-10): parses the SAME self._shopping_items_cache items with detect_currency + parse_price_string but has NO shopping_strict_currency_enabled() block — the R$ item converts BRL as USD (7411-7416) and the glyph item's raw amount is stamped `currency` (target) labelled local_bhd (7430-7434), then seeded into self._price_candidates where reconcile_pair_fairness can re-select and SHIP it. is_price_showable (7453) is a magnitude/provenance gate and cannot see the label error. So flipping M13-09 closes the front door but the wave's own back door (touched in the same commit, 40 lines of intent apart) still ships the 9.8x-mislabelled price on any tier1_shopping short-circuit followed by a fairness re-select.
fix: Mirror the two strict-shopping guards (letter-dollar USD un-detect + _shopping_foreign_currency_signal) inside the tier1_shopping loop of _seed_shortcircuit_candidates, gated on the same flag — or factor one shared per-item admission helper both paths call.
verify_reason: Re-derived in both files. price_service.py:9456-9473 applies the two strict guards (letter-dollar USD un-detect at :9461-9468, _shopping_foreign_currency_signal at :9469-9473) under shopping_strict_currency_enabled(). structured_comparison_service.py:7391-7439 (_seed_shortcircuit_candidates, rewritten by 033513e for M13-10) parses the SAME self._shopping_items_cache items with detect_currency + parse_price_string(display_text=True) and has NO strict block at all — the R$ item converts BRL as USD (:7407-7412) and the unresolved-glyph item is stamped `currency` (target) with source_method local_bhd (:7429-7434), then seeded into self._price_candidates for reconcile_pair_fairness. is_price_showable at :7453 is a magnitude/provenance gate and cannot see a label error. Not a re-file of M13-10 (report line 34 is the 1000x parse divergence, which the fix did close); this is the policy-parity gap the same wave left against M13-09. P2 is right: with ENABLE_SHOPPING_STRICT_CURRENCY default OFF the two paths agree today, so this is a pre-flip precondition, not a live bug.

title: ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD violates the pinned SIB-1 invariant: the guard pends only in build_comparison_response, so the SSE `prices` event flashes the region-mismatched price the final payload then pends
evidence: The M13-11 guard lives only in response_builder.py:1252-1267. The streaming `prices` event (structured_comparison_service.py:3794-3835) builds its payload through a deliberately MIRRORED pending projection whose own comment pins the invariant: 'the SSE prices event must use the SAME pending projection as the final complete response ... so an estimated/sample/wrong-cheap price the final card pends is never briefly flashed mid-stream' (3794-3798). That mirror applies is_price_showable (3819) but has no region-currency check, so with the flag ON a BHD adapter price on a saudi_arabia request is streamed in `prices` at progress 50 and then pended in settle_complete/complete — exactly the flash-then-retract the SIB-1 block exists to prevent, on the wave's own highest-blast-radius flag (runbook: canary LAST, alone).
fix: Mirror the region-currency pend into the SSE projection at scs:3814-3827 (resolve get_region_currency(region) once, pend when price.currency differs), or hoist both projections into one shared helper so the two surfaces cannot drift again.
verify_reason: Re-derived. The M13-11 guard exists at exactly one chokepoint: response_builder.py:1251-1267, inside build_comparison_response's pending loop. The SSE `prices` projection at structured_comparison_service.py:3794-3835 is the deliberate mirror whose own comment (:3794-3798) pins the SIB-1 invariant that it must use the SAME pending projection as the final complete response so a price the final card pends is never flashed mid-stream — and it applies only is_price_showable (:3819), with no region-currency check anywhere in the block. So with ENABLE_REGION_CURRENCY_GUARD ON, a BHD adapter price on a saudi_arabia request is streamed at the `prices` event and then pended in settle_complete/complete: flash-then-retract, on the flag CLAUDE.md:345 itself calls the highest-blast-radius change in the wave ('canary it LAST, alone'). Not an M13 row (M13-11 at report line 35 asked for the chokepoint guard; this is the second chokepoint the fix did not cover). P2 stands: the flag is default OFF, so it is a pre-flip precondition, but the flashed value is exactly the wrong-currency price M13-11 was filed to stop showing.

title: ThreadPoolExecutor-40 knee: 3rd concurrent cold fan-out queues; sustained >0.6-1.4 cold compares/s silently collapses price capture
evidence: Each cold compare launches ~18-24 to_thread adapter fetches (K=6 per mechanism x up to 8 mechanisms + shopify/algolia/sitemap/jsonapi selectors, source_router.py:821-844; prefetch fan-out structured_comparison_service.py:5560-5680). Pool = 40 (executor.py:30). Instantaneous: 2 fan-outs fit, the 3rd queues (54-72 demand vs 40). Throughput: 40/mean-hold → at 1.4s median (bake-off figure) = 28.5 fetches/s = 1.4 cold compares/s (85/min); at 3s realistic mean (some 9s-clamp walls) = 0.6/s (40/min). Because _timeout_none's 10s wrap timer runs while the task is QUEUED (adapter_timeouts.py:24), sustained arrival above pool drain burns queued adapters' whole budget in the queue within 30-60s — every adapter returns None, prices degrade to estimate/pend with zero errors, and a ~15-simultaneous-arrival burst alone pushes tail compares' queue wait past the 9s inner ceiling. With W3 offloads ON the same pool also absorbs ~50 Redis/DB calls x 163ms ≈ +8 thread-s/compare → ~36 thread-s/compare vs 40 thread-s/s capacity ≈ 1.1 cold compares/s ceiling unchanged.
fix: Quantified tuning guidance, not a code defect: (a) publish the knee (concurrent cold fan-outs > 2 queue; sustained > ~40-85 cold/min collapses capture) as the ADAPTER_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS sizing rule — workers ≈ 20 x target concurrent cold compares (+ ~10 x with offloads ON at current RTT); (b) add a saturation signal (queue depth or fetch-start latency histogram on the qaren-worker pool) so capture collapse is observable as saturation, not mistaken for source outages; (c) consider starting the wrap timer at thread-start rather than submit, or shedding (returning None immediately) when queue depth exceeds the race budget.
verify_reason: Pool=40 verified (executor.py:30) and the module's own docstring already records ~18 concurrent adapter fetches per compare with headroom for ~2 full fan-outs — matching the finding's 2-fit-3rd-queues claim (54-72 demand vs 40). K=6 per-mechanism cap verified (source_router.py:821-844, BH_GCC_FANOUT_K default 6); prefetch _timeout_none sites at scs:5629-5808 confirmed. The queued-timer mechanism is real: _timeout_none wraps the adapter coro in asyncio.wait_for (scs:208-227) and the adapter's to_thread future waits in the executor queue INSIDE that timer, so queue wait burns the 10s budget and returns None silently — though the citation should be scs:208/227 rather than adapter_timeouts.py:24 (that file is the mirror constant for inner clamps; minor imprecision, not a refutation). Throughput math re-derived correct: 40/1.4s=28.6 fetches/s → 1.4 cold/s; 40/3s → 0.67/s; a 15-compare burst ≈ 300 tasks → ~10.5s tail queue wait at 1.4s hold, past the 9s inner ceiling; flags-ON +50×163ms ≈ +8 thread-s/compare → ~1.1/s unchanged. The 1.4s 'median' leans on the bake-off's small sample, but the finding brackets 1.4-3s. Correctly scoped as tuning guidance vs M13-34's determinism fix. P2 stands.

title: Drain-not-abandon retains 100% of server work on disconnect; with the client's SSE-to-REST fallback one flaky tap can cost two full paid pipelines
evidence: On disconnect the generator sets client_gone and CONTINUES draining to completion (text_routes.py:556-570) — a client dropping at t=2s still costs the full cold pipeline: 15s Phase-1 race, the flags-off UNBOUNDED verdict/moderation tail, ~20k OpenAI tokens and 6-15 Serper credits (when armed), holding ~20 executor threads and loop slices for 15-45s (minutes under OpenAI degradation) with zero user value. The documented client fallback (api.ts streamComparison → non-streaming on failure, CLAUDE.md) then runs a SECOND full compare for the same tap. Load multiplier under flaky mobile ≈ 1/(1-r) per delivery: 1.25x at 20% drop-rate, 2.5x at 60%; capacity terms: at the 10-20/min admitted ceiling, a 30% drop-rate cohort wastes ~4-6 of those slots on invisible work. Pre-verdict drops refund the usage credit (usage_refund.text_stream.incomplete, :622-634) but not the upstream spend.
fix: Gate the drain on progress: if the disconnect happens BEFORE the verdict event (complete_response is None and no verdict yielded), cancel the generator instead of draining — metering integrity only requires the drain once the client could have received the result (the M13-35 scenario). Alternatively/additionally activate ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE so a drained tail is capped at the 30s residual, and have the mobile client suppress the non-streaming fallback when the SSE attempt reached the verdict event.
verify_reason: Code verified: on disconnect the generator sets client_gone and continues draining to completion (text_routes.py:556-570, the continue at :564/:568), the pre-verdict refund label usage_refund.text_stream.incomplete exists (:633), the flag-off tail it drains into is unbounded (scs:3936-3944/3965-3973), and the client's SSE→non-streaming fallback is documented (CLAUDE.md api.ts streamComparison), consuming a second slot from the same shared limiter bucket per LS-01. Multiplier arithmetic correct: 1/(1-r) = 1.25x at r=0.2, 2.5x at r=0.6. Duplication boundary examined closely because CLAUDE.md's W3 'M13-35 resource note' ALREADY states the amplification qualitatively (early connect-then-drop → full server-side compare; mitigations: gate drain on complete_response, or M13-04 ON) — so this is deliberately-accepted W3 behavior with a documented mitigation, not a missed defect. Not refuted as a duplicate because the lane's mandate is quantification of residuals, and the genuinely new content is (a) the retry-geometric load multiplier under flaky networks and (b) the SSE→REST fallback doubling demand exactly at the 429 ceiling — neither appears in M13-35 or its resource note. P2 appropriate: real load amplifier, but bounded by the compare-route rate limits that bind first (LS-01) and by ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE when flipped.

title: Freemium gate burns 2 Supabase + up to 6 Redis round trips serially inline before any compare work starts
evidence: consume_comparison_credit executes strictly sequentially on the loop: _get_user_tier_info (run_db inline, usage_service.py:290) then _get_active_referral_bonus (usage_service.py:360) then _atomic_consume 2x incrby + up to 3x decrby/expire (usage_service.py:163-176) then 2x _get_redis_count for the response shape (usage_service.py:251-252). Mid estimate ~500ms, worst ~1s, of pure serial pre-work per authed compare - it also delays the SSE stream's first event by the same amount (text_routes.py:424+ runs the same gate before yielding). The two Supabase reads are independent of each other and of the Redis consume, yet run one-by-one.
fix: With ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD ON the two run_db calls leave the loop but are still serial: gather tier-info and bonus concurrently (asyncio.gather), fold the 2 remaining-count GETs into the values incrby already returned (new_daily/new_monthly are the counts - the extra GETs are pure waste), and consider caching tier info per user for 60s.
verify_reason: Code verified: consume_comparison_credit (usage_service.py:199) awaits _get_user_tier_info (:214) then _get_active_referral_bonus (:217) strictly serially though they are independent, then _atomic_consume (:237, sync incrby x2 at :163/:169), then re-reads both counters via _get_redis_count (:251-252) even though the incrby return values at :163/:169 ARE those counts — the redundancy claim is exact. The gate runs before the SSE stream's first yield (same consume_comparison_credit call at text_routes.py:486). Mid estimate 2S+4R ≈ 500ms follows from the declared inputs. Not a duplicate: M13-37 filed the TOCTOU and created this shape; neither the serialization nor the redundant re-reads appear in any M13 row.

title: Token-revocation check is a blocking Redis GET on EVERY authed request and is in neither offload set
evidence: verify_token calls _is_token_revoked first (auth_service.py:249), which does redis_client.get(f'revoked:{sha}') on the blocking Upstash REST client (auth_service.py:306-315). Every authed endpoint (compare, stream, history, home, usage, auth/me, events...) pays a full Upstash RTT (~75-163ms) on the loop before the Supabase auth call. At ~6 authed requests per app-open+compare cycle that is ~0.45-1s of loop stall per user cycle from this one line. M13-05 wraps the client.auth.get_user call at auth_service.py:254 in run_db but the Redis read one line above it was left inline, and ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD's dispatch (scs._cache_get_async) does not reach auth_service.
fix: Wrap in the same run_db/to_thread dispatch (it is exactly the class of call M13-05 targets), or memoise negative lookups in-process for a few seconds (revocation latency tolerance is already 1h TTL), or move the blacklist to a per-process LRU refreshed async.
verify_reason: Verified precisely: verify_token calls _is_token_revoked at auth_service.py:249 BEFORE the run_db-wrapped Supabase call at :254; _is_token_revoked (:306-315) does a raw redis_client.get on the blocking Upstash REST client (cache_service.py:24-32, upstash_redis over HTTP; repo's own 163ms measurement at serper_service.py:213-216). It is in neither offload set — run_db wraps only the get_user lambda, and the _cache_get_async dispatch lives in structured_comparison_service with no auth_service caller. M13 adjacency correctly stated: M13-05's hot set covers the :254 Supabase call; M13-36 mentions _is_token_revoked but for fail-open observability (a different defect), so no filed row covers the per-authed-request loop stall. Every authed endpoint pays it; P2 stands.

title: /home/smart-pick pulls 5 complete full_response payloads (~0.25-1MB) through a sync execute on the loop
evidence: smart_pick on cache miss selects 'id, full_response, created_at' for the 5 most-recent v2 comparisons (home_routes.py:550-557) plus a users select (home_routes.py:509-514), sync client inside async def. 5 full comparison payloads is roughly 0.25-1MB => the S RTT inflates to 200ms-1s of loop stall, on an app-open endpoint with a 5-min TTL. _select_smart_pick needs only winner name/price/category - a tiny projection of each payload.
fix: Project the needed fields via jsonb path selection (or persist a small smart_pick_summary column at save time - the denormalized product_names column from migration 020 shows the pattern), wrap in run_db, and bust on save_comparison instead of a 5-min TTL.
verify_reason: Verified: smart_pick on cache miss runs a users select (home_routes.py:509-515) plus a 5-row select including full full_response payloads (:550-558), both sync executes inside async def, behind a 5-min TTL (_SMART_PICK_TTL_SECONDS = 5*60 at :54). The projection claim holds — _select_smart_pick consumes a small subset of each payload while the query ships the entire comparison JSON x5. M13 overlap claim verified by grep: zero rows mention home_routes or smart_pick. Bounded (limit 5) unlike LS-01, so P2 is the right severity; the 0.25-1MB payload figure is a declared estimate consistent with the repo's own full_response sizing.

title: Nobody filed the cheapest lever: a second uvicorn worker - the deployment is pinned to 1 loop by a start-command default, not by a design constraint
evidence: Procfile:1 and railway.json:7 omit --workers, so one blocking call parks the entire deployment. The M13 review states 'single-worker uvicorn' as Theme T4 context, and all four fix waves attack the blocking calls - none proposes worker scaling. The app is already largely multi-process-safe: per-request service instances (CLAUDE.md invariant), all shared state in Upstash/Supabase, no in-process locks on the request path. Known per-worker splits are bounded and benign: slowapi memory:// buckets (limits double per worker - the decorated 10/min becomes 10/min/worker), the SERPER_GATE_CACHE_TTL memo and serper-breaker memo become per-worker (bounded overshoot already documented as acceptable at serper_service.py:223-226), and the M13-34 executor is per-process. `--workers 2` halves rho at every N in the model (saturation ~10->~20 mixed) for one line, multiplicatively with the W3 offloads.
fix: Add --workers 2 (memory permitting - measure RSS first via railway metrics; each worker duplicates the app) to the start command as an explicit, documented capacity decision with the limiter-split caveat; re-verify the M13-34 ADAPTER_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS sizing per worker (40 threads x2). File it as a canary-able infra change alongside the W3 flag flips.
verify_reason: Verified: Procfile:1 and railway.json:7 both run bare 'uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT' — no --workers, no gunicorn. The M13 doc's only worker references are the T4 theme statement ('Single-worker uvicorn (no --workers in Procfile or railway.json)', line 256) used as context, and Wave 3's scope (:314-335) which proposes to_thread sweeps, wrappers, deadlines and an executor — never worker scaling; no M13-NN row files it. The multi-process-safety survey checks out: slowapi memory:// storage is per-process (rate_limiter.py:103-110, so decorated limits double per worker as stated), the serper gate/breaker memos are per-process with documented bounded overshoot (serper_service.py:223-226), shared state is in Upstash/Supabase, services are per-request instances. The caveats (RSS measurement first, executor sizing per worker, limiter split) are the right ones. A genuine remediation-plan gap; P2 appropriate.

title: Zero-HA topology with a hard restart budget: 1 replica x 1 worker, ON_FAILURE max 3 retries, then permanent downtime
evidence: railway.json:10-11 sets restartPolicyType ON_FAILURE with restartPolicyMaxRetries=3; environment_status shows a single active deployment (1 replica), start command runs 1 uvicorn worker. A crash-loop that passes the /health check (healthcheckTimeout 30s, railway.json:8-9 — /health is a no-I/O handler at app/main.py:307-313 so it validates nothing about DB/Redis) then dies under real traffic exhausts 3 restarts and leaves prod DOWN until a human redeploys. Exposure is amplified by deploy cadence: 20 deployments in ~51h measured (2026-08-30 02:16 -> 2026-09-01 04:54). No OOM/crash observed in the current deployment window (clean single container start 04:55:47) — this is a ceiling, not an incident.
fix: Raise restartPolicyMaxRetries (or switch to ALWAYS) for the web service, and make /health minimally dependency-aware (or add a separate /ready) so a wedged process fails the deploy-time check instead of cutting over. Consider 2 replicas only AFTER LS-railway-metrics-04 is resolved.
verify_reason: railway.json:7-11 verified: ON_FAILURE, restartPolicyMaxRetries=3, healthcheckPath /health with 30s timeout, single-worker start command; /health at main.py:307-313 verified no-I/O (validates nothing about DB/Redis). Not an M13 duplicate — no M13 row touches restart policy or replica topology, and the doc explicitly scopes out Railway service configuration beyond Procfile/railway.json. The single-replica claim and 20-deploys/51h cadence rest on Railway MCP reads I could not re-run (MCP unauthorized this session), but the cadence is consistent with 97 main commits landing in that window across the four fix waves, and the finding correctly labels itself 'a ceiling, not an incident'. P2 appropriate.

title: memory:// limiter storage makes horizontal scaling change rate-limit semantics (limits multiply per replica) and wipes state every deploy
evidence: _get_storage_uri hardcodes 'memory://' (rate_limiter.py:103-110) with an explicit 'acceptable for a single Railway instance' assumption. At today's 1 replica that holds, but: (a) any move to replicas>1 (the natural first response to the LS-railway-metrics-02 loop ceiling) silently multiplies every limit by the replica count and makes 429s load-balancer-nondeterministic — a scale blocker that must be fixed BEFORE adding replicas; (b) limiter state resets on every deploy — at the measured 20-deploys/51h cadence the brute-force windows on auth routes were wiped ~every 2.5h. Upstash REST incompatibility with slowapi's redis:// scheme is the stated reason.
fix: Before any multi-replica scale-out: back slowapi with a protocol-speaking Redis (Railway Redis addon or Upstash with TCP endpoint) or replace slowapi with an Upstash-REST token-bucket keyed per client. Sequence it with the M13-02 key fix — fixing the key while keeping memory:// still breaks at replicas>1.
verify_reason: rate_limiter.py:103-110 verified: hardcoded 'memory://' with the explicit 'acceptable for a single Railway instance' comment and the Upstash-REST-incompatibility rationale. The multi-replica semantics claim (per-process buckets multiply limits by replica count, 429s become LB-nondeterministic) follows correctly from in-memory storage. Deploy-wipes-limiter-state follows trivially; the ~2.5h figure re-derives (51h/20). The 'un-filed' claim verified by grep of the full M13 doc: M13-01 covers middleware registration and M13-02 the key_func — no row covers the storage backend or replica semantics, making this the strongest 'anything they missed' candidate in the lane. The sequencing note (key fix + memory:// still breaks at replicas>1) is correct. P2 appropriate as a scale-blocker rather than a today-defect.

title: 21 undecorated routes are unmetered today; worst are authenticated Supabase-blocking routes that amplify into whole-deployment event-loop stalls
evidence: SlowAPIMiddleware is registered only when _default_rate_limits_enabled() (main.py:137-138), and ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS is unset/OFF in prod, so default_limits never fire and the undecorated routes have NO limit. Enumerated: GET / (main.py:275), /health (:307), /favicon.ico (:267); GET /app/version (version_routes.py:19); GET /legal/{privacy,privacy_policy,terms,terms_of_service} (legal_routes.py:17-35); GET /url/retailers (url_routes.py:46); GET /usage/status (usage_routes.py:9); GET /referrals/status (referral_routes.py:239); auth POST /logout (auth_routes.py:549), GET /me (:563), GET /verify (:615), PUT /profile (:628), GET /preferences (:766), PUT /preferences (:813), GET /cohort-profile (:1073); admin-gated DELETE /text/cache (text_routes.py:805) + GET /text/parse (:840) which call parse_product_query→OpenAI. The authenticated DB routes (GET /me, GET /preferences, PUT /profile, PUT /preferences, GET /usage/status, GET /referrals/status, GET /auth/cohort-profile) each run a blocking sync Supabase .execute() on the single-worker asyncio loop (M13-05 hot set), so a single valid-token holder can issue unbounded DB round trips and stall unrelated requests into the 15s/30s wall-clock caps.
fix: Cannot safely fix via ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS until the key is per-client (arming it under the shared proxy IP 429s /health and app-open reads for everyone — the M13-01 precondition). Instead: decorate the authenticated DB routes with explicit per-route limits once proxy-aware keying lands, wrap their .execute() in asyncio.to_thread (ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD, M13-05), and confirm DELETE /text/cache + GET /text/parse stay admin-gated. Add lightweight caching/short limits to the anon static routes to blunt volumetric floods.
verify_reason: Mechanism and enumeration verified: SlowAPIMiddleware registered only under _default_rate_limits_enabled() (main.py:137-138, flag unset in prod), so default_limits never fire; every listed route confirmed undecorated at its cited line (main.py:267/275/307; version_routes.py:19; legal_routes.py:17-35; url_routes.py:46; usage_routes.py:9; referral_routes.py:239; auth_routes.py logout 548, /me 563, /verify 615, PUT /profile 628, GET/PUT /preferences 766/813, /cohort-profile 1073; text_routes.py:805/840 — both admin-gated via Depends(verify_admin_key) and both calling parse_product_query→OpenAI, exactly as characterized). The amplification chain is code-grounded, not speculation: db_offload.py's own M13-05 docstring states the identical mechanism, and with ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD OFF run_db executes .execute() inline on the loop (verify_token via auth_service.py:254, _get_user_tier_info/_get_active_referral_bonus in usage_service.py:478-481). GET /text/price-kpi correctly excluded (30/min + admin dep, text_routes.py:746-752). One arithmetic correction that does not change severity: the headline '21 undecorated routes' is M13-01's pre-W1 count — W1 decorated PUT /auth/email and PUT /auth/password at 5/min (auth_routes.py:661, 695) — and the finding's own correct enumeration totals 20 paths (18 handlers; the legal routes stack two paths per handler). Overlap with M13-01/M13-05 is declared; the rate-gap × loop-block composition and the observation that the shipped default-limits fix is itself unusable under the shared key are the quantification value-add. P2 appropriate.

title: slowapi memory:// storage resets every deploy/restart and is a latent multi-worker footgun
evidence: storage_uri='memory://' (rate_limiter.py:103-110), chosen because Upstash is REST and cannot serve slowapi's redis:// scheme. Buckets are in-memory per process. Two consequences at scale: (a) counters do NOT survive restarts — every Railway deploy, crash (railway.json restartPolicyMaxRetries 3), OOM or scale event wipes all slowapi minute-windows, so the credential-route brute-force windows M13-01/02 rely on reset on each deploy and an attacker can reset the window by triggering/waiting for a restart; (b) both start commands run a single worker (no --workers), which is the ONLY reason the buckets are coherent — adding --workers N later fragments buckets per worker, silently multiplying every limit by N and making enforcement nondeterministic (a request routed to a fresh worker sees a fresh counter), with no redis:// backend available to fix it.
fix: Document that limits are per-process and reset on deploy; keep uvicorn single-worker until a shared store exists. If horizontal scale or workers are needed, back slowapi with a redis:// store (a real Redis, or a redis-protocol shim) rather than Upstash-REST, or move limiting to Railway's edge. For credential brute-force durability, ensure the protective window (account lockout) is Redis-backed and not dependent on the volatile slowapi minute-window.
verify_reason: All inputs verified: storage_uri='memory://' returned at rate_limiter.py:110 with the explicit Upstash-is-REST-not-redis:// rationale in the comment (:105-108); single worker confirmed (no --workers in any of the four start commands); restartPolicyMaxRetries 3 confirmed in railway.json; account lockout confirmed as separate and Redis-backed with fail-open (check_account_locked, auth_service.py:540-548), so the slowapi minute-windows are indeed the only volatile layer and reset on every deploy/crash — an inherent property of per-process in-memory storage, correctly derived rather than claimed as measurement. The multi-worker fragmentation is presented as a latent conditional ('the moment anyone adds --workers N'), which is accurate limits/slowapi behavior, and the no-redis://-backend constraint follows from the Upstash-REST architecture. Novelty against M13 verified by search: zero hits for memory://, storage_uri, or counter-reset anywhere in docs/investigations/2026-08-31-m13-full-review.md; the doc's only single-worker mention (line 256) describes the deployment topology for the event-loop theme (M13-05/06/30-37), not limiter-storage coherence or deploy-reset. Genuinely new scale finding; P2 appropriate given it is today a documentation/latent risk rather than an active failure.

title: FE sends metadata.query as comparison_id — M13-29 UUID validators now 422-reject every ResultsScreen event batch and every feedback submission
evidence: ResultsScreen.tsx:331 `const comparisonId = metadata?.query;` — response_builder.py:1580 sets metadata.query to the raw query string ('iPhone 15 vs S24'), never a UUID; no compare payload carries a comparison id at all (save_comparison generates it post-hoc, database_service.py:214-226, and never injects it back). That string is attached to every tracked event (ResultsScreen.tsx:337, and unconditionally to result_view_duration at :379) and to FeedbackCard via feedbackComparisonId (ResultsScreen.tsx:711 → ResultsContent.tsx:547 → FeedbackCard.tsx:52-55). title: SSE 'error' event handler drops code/layer — CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE contract never fires on the streaming path and raw exception text leaks to the user
evidence: api.ts:475 `case 'error': callbacks.onError?.(new Error(parsed.error || 'Stream error'))` discards parsed.code and parsed.layer. Backend error events carry structure: content-safety yields {success:false, error, code:'CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE', layer:'query_prefilter'} (structured_comparison_service.py:3563-3568), and the generic streaming catch yields {success:false, error:str(e)} with an arbitrary Python exception string (:4176-4180). HomeScreen.onError branches on parseApiError(error).code==='CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE' (HomeScreen.tsx:362) and reads error?.response?.data?.layer (:363) — both undefined for a bare Error, so the Bundle B content-block Alert/analytics path never fires on streams; execution falls to HomeScreen.tsx:381 `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), error.message || …)`, which renders the backend string verbatim — for the generic catch that is str(e) (e.g. 'TypeError: …'), violating the no-scary-copy contract. Contrast the complete/success:false path which carefully preserves code via a synthetic axios-shaped error (api.ts:459-465).
fix: Mirror the complete-event pattern on the error event: `callbacks.onError?.(Object.assign(new Error(parsed.error || 'Stream error'), { response: { status: 503, data: { code: parsed.code, error: parsed.error, layer: parsed.layer } } }))` so parseApiError/isUsageLimitError/CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE branching works identically on both terminal shapes, and never surface error.message when a code is present.
verify_reason: api.ts:475 is verbatim `case 'error': callbacks.onError?.(new Error(parsed.error || 'Stream error')); break;` - code and layer discarded, in direct contrast to the complete-event path at api.ts:459-465 which builds a synthetic axios-shaped error to preserve code. Backend error events do carry structure: structured_comparison_service.py:3564-3568 yields {success:False, error, code:'CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE', layer:'query_prefilter'} (before the try block, so it reaches the SSE stream), and the generic catch at :4177-4180 yields {'success': False, 'error': str(e), ...}. text_routes.py:517-522 is event-type-agnostic and passes both through. On the client, parseApiError (api.ts:619-651) reads only error.response.data, so a bare Error yields code null and message = error.message; HomeScreen.tsx:362 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE branch and :363 layer read never fire, and execution reaches HomeScreen.tsx:381 `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), error.message || ...)` rendering str(e) verbatim - a no-scary-copy contract violation. P2 correct.
