title: performRefresh discards refreshSession()'s result and reports success whenever ANY token is still stored — the 401 retry replays the identical dead token
evidence: performRefresh (api.ts:49-63) does `await refreshSession(); const newToken = await getToken(); if (newToken) return { success: true, token: newToken }` — it never inspects refreshSession()'s return value. refreshSession resolves (does NOT throw) with `{success:false}` on three separate paths that leave the stale access token in SecureStore: no refresh token (authService.ts:218), backend replies 200 without a session (authService.ts:243), and any non-401 error incl. offline (authService.ts:254-257). In all three, getToken() still returns the EXPIRED access token, so the interceptor takes the success branch (api.ts:116-118), sets `Authorization: Bearer <same dead token>` and replays the request, which 401s again; `_retry` is already true (api.ts:112) so it rejects. Net effect: the documented 'auto-refresh on 401' silently degrades to 'retry once with the token that just failed', and callers get a raw 401 rejection they interpret as a request failure rather than a session failure.
fix: Gate on the refresh result, not on the presence of a token: `const r = await refreshSession(); if (!r.success) { await clearSession(); return { success:false, token:null }; }` — and treat the non-401 (network) failure as a retryable transient rather than a successful refresh.
verify_reason: Mechanism re-derived and correct. api.ts:49-63 `await refreshSession(); const newToken = await getToken(); if (newToken) return {success:true,...}` — the result object is never inspected. authService.ts:218 (no refresh token), :243 (`return {success:false, error:'Refresh failed'}` when the 200 body has no session) and :254-257 (non-401/network) all resolve false while leaving the old access token in SecureStore, so the interceptor takes the success branch at api.ts:116-118 and replays with the dead token. Only the 401 branch (authService.ts:248-250) clears, making getToken() null and the interceptor reject correctly. Not a re-file of M13-57 (that is identifyFromImages bypassing the interceptor). Downgraded from P1: the observable delta versus correct behaviour is one extra doomed HTTP request plus a stale-session record that is not cleared — the caller receives the same 401 rejection either way (`_retry` is already true at api.ts:112), so no user-visible outcome changes on its own. The lockout consequence the finding leans on belongs to MB-flows-02, not to this defect.

title: No path back to Auth after a session is cleared mid-session — the app keeps rendering Main with no token
evidence: `isAuthenticated` is only ever set false by handleLogout (App.tsx:233-238), and handleLogout is passed to exactly two screens: HistoryScreen (App.tsx:128 → HistoryScreen.tsx:730) and ProfileScreen (App.tsx:139 → ProfileScreen.tsx:311). Nothing else can flip it. But clearSession() fires from two non-UI places: performRefresh's catch (api.ts:59-61) and refreshSession's 401 branch (authService.ts:248-250). After either, the navigator still renders MainTabs. ResultsScreen even encodes the false assumption: on a 401 it does nothing at all with the comment `Axios 401 interceptor handles refresh/redirect — no-op here` (ResultsScreen.tsx:205-206) — there is no redirect anywhere in the codebase. Concretely: token expires while backgrounded, refresh token is revoked → every Home compare ends in an Alert (HomeScreen.tsx:381), every history row opens as 'No comparison loaded' (ResultsScreen.tsx:607-651, loadError stays null), the camera path reports 'vision_failed'. The only escape is discovering the History tab, whose 401 branch shows the sign-in card (HistoryScreen.tsx:723-736), or force-quitting the app.
fix: Lift the auth-invalidation signal out of the interceptor: have clearSession/performRefresh publish a 'session-invalid' event (or expose an onUnauthenticated callback from App.tsx) that calls handleLogout, so any 401 that survives refresh returns the user to the Auth stack from whatever screen they are on.
verify_reason: Confirmed as a code fact with one correction. `setIsAuthenticated(false)` appears only in handleLogout (App.tsx:233-238); handleLogout is wired to three places, not two — HistoryScreen (App.tsx:128), ProfileScreen (App.tsx:139) and EditProfileScreen `onAccountDeleted` (App.tsx:334) — all user-initiated. Nothing in api.ts/authService signals App.tsx, so clearSession from api.ts:59-61 or authService.ts:248-250 leaves MainTabs mounted with no token, and ResultsScreen.tsx:205-206 comments that the interceptor 'handles refresh/redirect' when no redirect exists anywhere. Downgraded from P1 because two real escapes exist and both are verified in code: HistoryScreen's 401 branch renders the sign-in card wired to onLogout (HistoryScreen.tsx:358-361, 723-736), and any cold start returns to the Auth stack because initializeAuth returns null when user/token are cleared (authService.ts:365-368). No data loss, no security exposure — a stuck-until-restart degraded state on Home/Results.

title: Registration that needs email confirmation reports success and then silently dead-ends on the Register screen
evidence: register() keys success on `response.data.user` alone and returns `token: response.data.session?.access_token` — which is undefined when Supabase requires email confirmation; the code even logs that case (authService.ts:114-129, warn at :120). RegisterScreen then takes the success branch and calls onRegisterSuccess() (RegisterScreen.tsx:208-209) → App.handleLoginSuccess → verifyAuth() → initializeAuth, which returns null at `if (!user || !token) return null` (authService.ts:368). handleLoginSuccess's entire body is inside `if (authUser)` (App.tsx:215-227), so nothing happens: no setIsAuthenticated, no error, no navigation. `finally { setLoading(false) }` (RegisterScreen.tsx:216) clears the spinner and the user is left staring at the same filled-in form with no message. Tapping Create account again now hits the backend's 'already registered' error, so the user's only signal is a contradictory failure on a second attempt.
fix: Return the confirmation state from register() (e.g. `{success:true, needsEmailConfirmation:true}` when no access_token) and render a 'check your inbox' screen; independently, make handleLoginSuccess surface the `authUser === null` case instead of no-oping.
verify_reason: Chain re-derived exactly: register() returns success on `response.data.user` alone with `token: response.data.session?.access_token` (authService.ts:113-128, dev warn at :120 naming the email-confirmation case); RegisterScreen.tsx:208-209 branches on result.success and calls onRegisterSuccess(); App.handleLoginSuccess wraps its whole body in `if (authUser)` (App.tsx:215-227); verifyAuth → initializeAuth returns null at `if (!user || !token) return null` (authService.ts:365-368) because saveToken was skipped. So the screen silently no-ops with the spinner cleared — confirmed. Downgraded from P1 because the trigger is unverifiable from the repo and appears not to be active: it fires only when Supabase returns a user without a session (email confirmation on). The backend has an 'email not confirmed' login mapping (auth_service.py:46) but nothing forces confirmation at register, and the app has live registered users. Latent, high-blast-radius-if-enabled, so P2 not P1. The secondary half — handleLoginSuccess swallowing `authUser === null` — is real regardless.

title: Onboarding completion persistence is fire-and-forget with no retry or local draft, so a failed save silently loses every answer and re-runs all 17 steps on the next launch
evidence: safeFire() swallows every rejection (NewOnboardingHost.tsx:67-76) and handleComplete calls onComplete(data) unconditionally afterwards (`Always advance the user, even if the network is offline`, :122-130). The gate that decides whether onboarding runs is server-side: App.tsx:194 sets `needsPreferences = !authUser.preferences_completed`, and the ONLY writer of that column is save_user_preferences (app/services/auth_service.py:477-480), reached solely through the savePreferences call at NewOnboardingHost.tsx:111. So when that PUT fails (offline, the 400 raised at app/api/auth_routes.py:841-842, or a 401 from a session that just went stale) the user is advanced into Main with no preferences stored, the ±30% explicit personalization silently inactive, and `preferences_completed` still false — the next cold start drops them at step 1 of 17 again with no explanation. Nothing is queued, retried or cached: OnboardingFlow holds `data` in component state only (OnboardingFlow.tsx:206).
fix: Await the three saves with a short timeout before advancing; on failure persist {step, data} to AsyncStorage and retry on next foreground (the rehydrate hooks already exist as initialStep/initialData, OnboardingFlow.tsx:91-93), and only clear the draft once savePreferences returns success.
verify_reason: Every link verified. safeFire swallows all rejections (NewOnboardingHost.tsx:67-76); handleComplete fires the three saves with `void safeFire(...)` and then calls onComplete unconditionally under the comment 'Always advance the user, even if the network is offline' (:111, :122-130). The gate is server-side: App.tsx:194/222 sets needsPreferences from `!authUser.preferences_completed`, and the only writer of that column is save_user_preferences (app/services/auth_service.py:476-480, `admin.table('users').update({'preferences': ..., 'preferences_completed': True})`), reachable only from the savePreferences call in handleComplete. So a failed PUT advances the user with no preferences stored and the gate still armed — next cold start restarts at step 1 with no draft anywhere (no AsyncStorage write on this path). Distinct from M13-61, which is the Arabic step-2 hard reload; this is the completion-time save. P2 is the right level: recoverable by redoing onboarding, no data loss beyond the answers.

title: ResultsScreen classifies failures by HTTP status only, so an offline or 5xx failure is reported as the user's fault and offers no retry
evidence: Camera path: the catch special-cases only USAGE_LIMIT and 503/TIMEOUT, then falls through to `setLoadError('vision_failed')` (ResultsScreen.tsx:272-295). Everything else lands there — an offline fetch (identifyFromImages uses raw fetch, api.ts:167, so a network drop throws a bare TypeError with no `response`) and every non-503 server error (api.ts:205 throws `new Error('Server error ' + status)`, again with no `response` field, so `err?.response?.status` is undefined). The user is then told `results.emptyState.visionFailed` = 'Snap each product in its own photo and we'll line them up side by side' (ResultsScreen.tsx:629-630) — i.e. blamed for their photos while the backend is down — and the only CTA is goBack (:638-646, the retry affordance is gated on `isTimeout`), so the natural recovery is to re-shoot and re-upload two images, which fails identically. History path: the same `else → setLoadError('generic')` (:211-213) turns an offline row-tap into the permanent 'No comparison loaded' + 'Back to history' with no retry.
fix: Add an explicit offline/transport branch (no `err.response` ⇒ connectivity) and a 5xx branch, both routed to the existing soft retryable state (loadError 'timeout' already has copy + handleRetry), and reserve 'vision_failed' for an actual `action === 'error'` response from /image/identify.
verify_reason: Re-derived in full. Camera catch (ResultsScreen.tsx:272-295) special-cases only `err.code === 'USAGE_LIMIT'` and `status === 503 || code === 'TIMEOUT'/'STREAM_TIMEOUT'`, then falls to `setLoadError('vision_failed')`. identifyFromImages uses raw fetch (api.ts:167-174) so an offline drop throws a bare TypeError with no `.response`, and every non-429 server error throws `new Error('Server error ' + status + ': ' + text)` (api.ts:205) — also no `.response` — so both land on vision_failed. The rendered copy is en `results.emptyState.visionFailed` = "Snap each product in its own photo and we'll line them up side by side." and the CTA is goBack, since both the body line and handleRetry are gated on `isTimeout` (ResultsScreen.tsx:612, 634-644). History path mirrors it with `else setLoadError('generic')` (:211-213). M13-57 covers only the 401 sub-case of the raw-fetch bypass; the offline/5xx misattribution and the missing retry affordance are untouched by it.

title: Any mid-stream SSE failure silently re-runs the entire comparison as a non-streaming GET, double-metering the user's freemium quota
evidence: The whole read loop lives inside one try (api.ts:410-481) and the catch treats every throw as 'SSE unavailable' and issues a fresh full compare, `api.get('/api/v1/text/compare', ...)` (api.ts:482-512). That catch is reached not only when the initial fetch fails but when `reader.read()` throws partway through — after status/specs/prices events have already been delivered and the backend has already run (and metered) the compare. The replacement GET is a second complete server-side comparison against the same quota, so one flaky-network compare can burn 2 of a free user's 3 lifetime comparisons. The user sees none of this: HomeScreen's caption stays frozen on the last streamed status (HomeScreen.tsx:318) under a full-screen `pointerEvents="auto"` overlay (HomeScreen.tsx:856-865) for up to the axios 120s timeout (api.ts:20) on top of the stream time, with no cancel affordance.
fix: Only fall back when the stream failed BEFORE any event was consumed (track a `receivedAnyEvent` flag); once events have arrived, surface the existing soft timeout state instead of re-running the compare. Separately, give the loading overlay a visible cancel that calls the returned abort().
verify_reason: Verified end to end, and the backend makes it worse than the finding states rather than better. The read loop and the fetch share one try (api.ts:~400-481); the catch returns early only on AbortError and otherwise issues a fresh `api.get('/api/v1/text/compare', ...)` (api.ts:482-512), so a `reader.read()` throw after events have been consumed re-runs a full compare. I checked whether M13-37's refund saves it: it does not in this window. text_routes.py:481-497 consumes a credit at the stream gate, but on client disconnect the generator sets `client_gone = True` and `continue`s to 'keep draining so the final payload is captured' (~:560-566); if the orchestrator then produces `complete_response`, the finally block takes the success branch — log_search, save_comparison and `record_lifetime_comparison` (~:596-604) — with no refund. The fallback GET then consumes a second credit at its own gate (:331-346) and records a second lifetime comparison (:405-417); the cache does not help because the consume happens before compare_from_text. So one flaky-network compare can meter twice, including against the lifetime free cap. The dead-abort sub-issue is filed elsewhere and is not what I am confirming here.

title: History hero marquee taps are a silent no-op for any recent decision not in the loaded page, including one the user just deleted
evidence: The marquee is fed by /profile/recent-decisions (HistoryScreen.tsx:113-115) but its tap handler resolves the id against the separately-fetched history list and bails when it misses: `const found = history.find((h) => h.id === id); if (found) viewAsResult(found);` (:762-767). Nothing in viewAsResult needs the row object — it only passes `item.id` (:426) — so the lookup exists purely to drop taps. It misses whenever the two endpoints disagree: a recent decision beyond the 50-row page (see MB-flows-07), a search filter active (the list is filtered, the marquee is not), or a row the user just deleted, since handleDelete only mutates the `history` array (:441) and HistoryHeroStats fetches once on mount (`useEffect([])`, :108-119) so the deleted comparison stays in the marquee. Tapping it does nothing at all — no navigation, no message.
fix: Navigate with the id directly (`navigation.navigate('Results', { comparison_id: id })`) instead of requiring a local row, and refetch or prune the hero data after a successful delete.
verify_reason: Re-derived. The marquee comes from getProfileRecentDecisions inside HistoryHeroStats, fetched once under `useEffect(..., [])` (HistoryScreen.tsx:108-119), while the tap handler resolves against the separately fetched page: `const found = history.find((h) => h.id === id); if (found) viewAsResult(found);` (:762-767). viewAsResult uses only `item.id` — `navigation.navigate('Results', { comparison_id: item.id })` (:426) — so the lookup is pure gatekeeping with no purpose. Divergence is reachable today, not only past 50 rows: after a search submit, loadHistory refetches filtered rows (:356) while the mount-only marquee keeps the unfiltered set, and handleDelete mutates only the `history` array (:441) so a just-deleted comparison stays tappable in the marquee. Either way the tap produces nothing — no navigation, no message. Adjacent to but not a re-file of M13-70, which is about stale numbers on HomeEditorialSections.

title: ContactUs localizes the category prefix, so the documented '[Bug]' operator grep never matches Arabic reporters

title: Compare abort path exists but has zero callers — in-flight compare survives unmount/logout and setState fires on a dead screen
evidence: Repo-wide grep for 'abort' shows only: api.ts:389/539 (AbortController + abort export) and HomeScreen.tsx:112/313/324/352 (abortRef declared, assigned, nulled twice). abortRef.current is NEVER invoked — no unmount cleanup (the only unmount effect, HomeScreen.tsx:187-194, clears just advanceTimerRef), no cancel affordance on the fullscreen loader (HomeScreen.tsx:856-865, pointerEvents='auto', no button), and the onError path (352-359) nulls the ref without aborting. title: ProductImage decodes full-resolution og:image bitmaps into 64-160px tiles — no resizeMethod, no expo-image, dozens of oversized decodes per History/Home screen

title: Sentry breadcrumb scrubbing is dead code: wrong event shape, and the unit test pins the wrong shape
evidence: sentry.ts:100 guards the breadcrumb scrub with `if (event.breadcrumbs && Array.isArray(event.breadcrumbs.values))`. In the installed SDK (@sentry/react-native 7.2.0 -> @sentry/core 10.12.0) the Event type declares `breadcrumbs?: Breadcrumb[]` (node_modules/@sentry/core/build/types/types-hoist/event.d.ts:45) — a plain ARRAY, so `event.breadcrumbs.values` resolves to Array.prototype.values (a function) and Array.isArray() is false: the entire breadcrumb message+data scrub NEVER executes on a real event. The shape `{values:[...]}` is the PYTHON SDK shape (backend sentry_service.py:154-159), copied during the parity mirror. The test suite green-lights the dead code because src/services/__tests__/sentry.test.ts:72-81 constructs the same wrong `{breadcrumbs:{values:[...]}}` fixture. Consequence: default fetch/XHR breadcrumbs attach full request URLs to every subsequent error event, and the SSE compare URL embeds user-typed search text (api.ts:411 `/api/v1/text/compare/stream?q=<user text>`), so user queries ship to Sentry unscrubbed while CLAUDE.md documents the mobile scrubber as 'Mirrors backend before_send scrub'. Re-derive: `node -e "const e={breadcrumbs:[{message:'Bearer abc.def'}]}; console.log(Array.isArray(e.breadcrumbs.values))"` prints false.
fix: Handle the real shape: `const crumbs = Array.isArray(event.breadcrumbs) ? event.breadcrumbs : event.breadcrumbs?.values; for (const crumb of crumbs ?? []) {...}` — and fix the test fixture to use `breadcrumbs: [...]` (array) so it fails on the current code before the fix and passes after.
verify_reason: Mechanics independently re-derived and all true: node_modules/@sentry/core (10.12.0 exactly as claimed) declares Event.breadcrumbs as a plain Breadcrumb[] (event.d.ts:45); sentry.ts:100 guards on Array.isArray(event.breadcrumbs.values) which is false for a real array (verified via node); the test fixture at src/services/__tests__/sentry.test.ts:73-80 pins the Python-SDK {values:[...]} shape (matching backend sentry_service.py:154-159); breadcrumbsIntegration() is in @sentry/react-native's default integrations so fetch URLs land in breadcrumbs; api.ts SSE URL carries q=<user text>. Not a duplicate of M13-56 (which is the message/extra gap). Severity downgraded P1->P2 for calibration with the M13 review's own scale: M13-56 — actual token-prefix diagHead plus verbatim server text shipping unredacted to the SAME Sentry sink — was rated P2. The consequence here (user search queries in breadcrumb URLs to the team's own write-only Sentry org) is the same class: a documented-control failure and PII-hygiene defect, not attacker-exploitable and not user-facing, which is what M13's P1 tier was reserved for.

title: Certificate pin set has no RSA-chain backup (ISRG Root X1 / R-series absent) — a repeat of the documented 2026-07-06 brick is one CA profile change away
evidence: All 5 pinned SPKI hashes (certificatePinning.ts:26-31, applied :42-48) sit on Let's Encrypt's ECDSA chain: ISRG Root X2 + intermediates YE1/E7/E8/E5. Let's Encrypt's RSA issuance path (R10-R14 intermediates chaining to ISRG Root X1) shares NONE of these keys, so if Railway's ACME client ever receives an RSA leaf (LE key-profile change, Railway TLS stack change, or an LE incident forcing E-series revocation) every backend HTTPS call fails closed and the app bricks. This exact failure already happened once: line 29's own comment records '2026-07-06: Railway rotated to LE intermediate YE1 (E5/E7/E8 no longer in chain) -> app bricked with Network Error'. Recovery is OTA-able (pins are JS-config; u.expo.dev is not pinned) but still means a full outage window plus the documented two-launch propagation delay for every installed device.
fix: Add the ISRG Root X1 SPKI pin (extract via the openssl runbook in the file header against https://letsencrypt.org/certs/isrgrootx1.pem) as a 6th backup hash. Pinning both LE roots covers every current LE issuance path; keep the E/YE pins for defense-in-depth.
verify_reason: Re-derived from certificatePinning.ts:26-48: all five pinned SPKI hashes are labeled ISRG Root X2 + LE YE1/E7/E8/E5 — every one on Let's Encrypt's ECDSA issuance family; the ISRG Root X1 (RSA root) pin is absent, so an RSA leaf from Railway's ACME client fails closed on every backend call. The in-file comment at line 29 documents that this exact failure mode already bricked the app once on 2026-07-06 when the intermediate rotated. Recovery is OTA-able (pins are JS config scoped to the Railway host only; u.expo.dev unpinned) but still a full outage plus the documented two-launch propagation delay. Not a duplicate: M13-112 covers only the un-awaited init call. P2 appropriate for a one-CA-profile-change total-outage with a documented precedent and a one-line fix.

title: verify_review_sentiment raises TypeError on a string average_rating at an unguarded call site, failing the entire product side
evidence: `deviation = abs(gpt_rating - serper_avg)` (:126) assumes numeric; the only guard is `gpt_rating is None` (:110). Probe: {'average_rating': '4.5'} -> TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'str' and 'float'. extract_reviews never coerces average_rating (extraction_service.py:1652-1669 only defaults source_ratings), the JSON-mode model can emit a quoted number, and cached reviews replay the same value for 7-14 days. title: Extractor picks the 1ml sample offer over the real bottle and drops JSON-LD availability

The real hole is the CASCADE: the JSON-LD rung correctly declined on multiplicity, and a lower rung then served the ambiguous price anyway — the page's `og:price:amount content="4.00"` meta (Shopify's cheapest-variant default) via the OG/microdata branch at :12840-12878, which is why in_stock is None (that branch never sees the Offer availability) and why `price_confirmed_in_text` is stamped (_cross_check_price at :12851, a non-JSON-LD-only call site). Fix belongs at the cascade: a JSON-LD multiplicity pend must suppress the OG/microdata rungs, not be silently overridden by them. title: _normalize_price kept the undampened 70-point cliff the A1 work removed from every other dim - a 1% price gap reads as decisive

The 70pt phantom feeds the value formula at 0.30-0.55 coefficient (21-38.5pt swing in the value dim from a 0.4-BHD delta), which exceeds the 5pt tradeoff filter (line 2006) and the 3pt dim-winner tie margin — so a near-identical price manufactures a 'value' dimension win, a tradeoff-pair entry, and (in electronics/other where the badge is live) a great_value/fair_price badge flip between near-identical prices. title: W3: refund recomputes date-keyed counters at refund time - midnight/month rollover burns the old credit and mints a negative one in the new window

title: M13-40 third JSON-LD pass (LIVE via default-ON ENABLE_JSONLD_FIRST) lets candidates in DIFFERENT currencies compete on raw numeric amount — smallest-numeral currency wins, not the right offer

Selection then ranks them numerically: select_best's last tiebreak is `amount` — 'with the exact gate OFF ... its ONLY rule' (comment at 10956-10958) — and the no-query fallback is `min(candidates, key=lambda c: c["amount"])` (10975). 45.00 EUR vs 170 SAR vs 6300 EGP for the SAME product compares 45 < 170 < 6300, so the pick is whichever currency prints the smallest numeral; the arbitrary winner is then converted downstream (13043-13054) and shipped as converted_usd, cached 7 days. The pre-wave invariant that made the amount tiebreak coherent — all candidates share expected_currency — is precisely what the pass lifts. The corpus gate showed only 3 amount changes because it has no multi-currency-offer pages.
fix: Normalise before ranking on the accept-any pass: convert each candidate's amount to a common unit (BHD via effective_fallback_rates) for comparison only, or partition candidates by currency and adjudicate multiplicity when more than one currency survives (pend rather than silently pick).

title: M13-09 strict-shopping over-pends two genuine shapes: 'US$ 25.99' (letter-dollar regex matches the S of US) and Arabic-Indic-numeral target-glyph prices (digits not stripped from the residue)

(a) price_service.py:9345 _LETTER_DOLLAR_RE=r'[A-Za-z]\$' and :9347 _BARE_DOLLAR_RE=r'(?<![A-Za-z])\$': for 'US$ 25.99' I get detect_currency='USD', letter_dollar=True, bare_dollar=False → the :9461-9468 condition is True → `continue`, i.e. a standard international USD notation whose detection was CORRECT is pended (parse_price_string returns a clean 25.99). title: ENABLE_EXTENDED_FALLBACK_RATES does not reach the direct-adapter convertibility gates — a TRY/PLN/CAD-base store still skips with the flag ON, so a canary of the flag will under-measure it

title: refund_comparison_credit across a UTC day/month rollover decrements the NEW window's key to -1, permanently: the -1 key never gets a TTL and offsets that user's counter forever
evidence: Keys are date-stamped at CALL time (usage_service.py:118-125: usage:daily:{user}:{YYYY-MM-DD}). A compare consumed before UTC midnight (~3am Bahrain) that fails after it (streams legitimately run 30-150s; the refund is fire-and-forget) refunds via _safe_decr (:152-157) against the NEW day's key: DECRBY on a missing key creates it at -1 with NO TTL, and the TTL branch in _atomic_consume (:163-167) only fires when INCRBY returns exactly 1 — incrementing from -1 returns 0, so the key NEVER receives an expiry. Result per occurrence: the old day's burned credit is not actually refunded, the new day silently grants one extra compare, and a permanent usage:daily key leaks. Same mechanics for the monthly key at month rollover.
fix: Capture the resolved daily/monthly key names at consume time and refund those exact keys (pass them through the return dict), and/or make _safe_decr skip when the key does not exist (Lua GET-then-DECR or DECR followed by a >=0 check with delete-on-negative).
verify_reason: The core defect is real, but one sub-claim in the evidence is wrong and the title overstates it. Real: usage_service.py:118-125 date-stamps _daily_key/_monthly_key at CALL time, and refund_comparison_credit (:258-268) recomputes them, so a compare consumed before UTC midnight and refunded after (streams legitimately run 30-150s and the refund is fire-and-forget) decrements the NEW window's key — the burned credit is not actually refunded and the new day silently starts at -1, granting the user one extra compare. REFUTED sub-claim: 'the key NEVER receives an expiry'. _atomic_consume:163-165 sets the TTL when INCRBY returns exactly 1; from -1 the first consume returns 0 (no TTL) but the SECOND returns 1 and _safe_expire(daily_key, 86400) does fire, so the key is not permanent for any user who makes two compares that day, and 'offsets that user's counter forever' does not hold. Residual leak is limited to the exactly-one-compare-that-day case. P3 stands (rare window, error favours the user), but the row should be retitled without 'permanently/forever'.

title: POST/GET /compare burn the reserved credit on an uncaught raise: refund fires only on a success:false RESULT, so any exception out of compare_from_text (or the post-gate plumbing) → 500 with the credit kept
evidence: consume_comparison_credit reserves at the gate (text_routes.py:173, 333); the only refund on the sync surfaces sits inside `if result.get('success') is False:` (:224-228 POST, :375-380 GET). An exception raised between the gate and the return — an unexpected raise inside compare_from_text that its internal catches miss, or a raise in the post-gate request plumbing — propagates to the error handler as a 500 and no refund path exists (no try/finally around the work, unlike the streaming route whose finally+else-refund covers exactly this). Pre-W3 the legacy flow metered only after success, so a 500 never burned a credit; the wave's atomic-consume made the raise path strictly worse for the user. Low frequency (compare_from_text catches broadly) but a deterministic conversion of every sync-surface 500 into a burned daily credit for free-tier users (3/day).
fix: Wrap the work in try/except (or try/finally with a success flag) on POST and GET: on any raise, fire the same usage_refund fire-and-forget before re-raising — mirroring the streaming finally's else-refund.
verify_reason: Re-derived at both sync surfaces. text_routes.py:173 (POST) and :333 (GET) reserve the credit via consume_comparison_credit with usage_consumed set at :184; the ONLY refund sits inside `if not result.get('success'):` at :205 → :226-229 (POST) and the mirrored block for GET. There is no try/except or try/finally wrapping the await service.compare_from_text(...) call at :192-202, so an exception escaping compare_from_text (or raised in the post-gate plumbing before the failure branch) propagates to the error handler as a 500 with the credit kept — unlike the streaming route, whose finally at :571 has an else-branch refund (:626-634) covering exactly the raise case. Correctly noted as low frequency (compare_from_text catches broadly) and correctly filed P3. Not a re-file: M13-37 (report line 66) is the TOCTOU, and the wave's dispatcher must-fix moved the refund ahead of _surface_comparison_failure only for the returned-failure shape.

title: GIL/CPU parse convoy is an unmodeled ceiling: 40 threads parsing up-to-3MB pages contend with the event loop for one GIL
evidence: Adapter fetches return up to max_bytes=3MB of HTML each (price_service.py:13879, truncation at :13940) and extract_price_from_html runs JSON-LD/microdata/regex passes over them inside executor threads; curl releases the GIL during network I/O but the parse phase holds it. Estimate: 100-300ms of pure-Python parse per page x ~20 pages = 2-6 GIL-seconds per cold compare, serialized across ALL 40 workers AND the event-loop thread on single-worker uvicorn (start command has no --workers). That puts the GIL ceiling at ~0.2-0.5 cold compares/s — the same order as the pool and loop ceilings — and, worse, parse bursts stall the LOOP (convoy effect), eroding the 15s race and SSE liveness for unrelated requests even below the ceiling. No M13 row models CPU/GIL; the byte-identity corpus gate is timing-blind to it.
fix: Measure before tuning: run the existing zero-network corpus (_proof, 414 pages) under py-spy/cProfile to get real per-page parse CPU, then either (a) cap concurrent PARSE (small semaphore) separately from fetch, (b) pre-slice HTML to the ld+json/script regions before full-document regex passes, or (c) plan a second uvicorn worker (2 processes halves the convoy at the cost of duplicated caches/limiters — note memory:// slowapi buckets would then double).
verify_reason: The direction is real (unmodeled CPU parse cost sharing one GIL with the loop; no M13 row covers it) but the finding's mechanism is factually wrong at its own cited paths and its magnitude is unsourced. (1) extract_price_from_html does NOT run 'inside executor threads': at every request-path call site it runs ON the event loop after the awaited fetch — price_service.py:13975-13982 (html = await curl_fetch_html_same_site(...) then a direct call), scs:1460, scs:2681 — so the '40 threads parsing vs one GIL' convoy model is misdescribed (the actual behavior — parse directly blocking the loop — is a different, arguably simpler stall mechanism that belongs inside LS-02's loop budget, not a separate 40-thread GIL convoy). (2) The '~20 pages × 100-300ms' inputs are both speculation: the ~18-24 fan-out is dominated by JSON-API adapters (woo/salla/occ/magento-gql/unbxd/rest_json/shopify products.json) that never call the HTML extractor, so far fewer than 20 full-HTML parses occur per cold compare; and 100-300ms/page has no measurement anywhere in the repo. The derived ceiling '~0.2-0.5 cold compares/s — same order as the pool and loop ceilings' is therefore a number built from two unsourced factors, presented alongside measured ceilings. Per the lane rule (a claim without a source is speculation), downgrade P2→P3: keep it as a profiling task (the fix's py-spy-over-corpus step is right), not a ranked capacity ceiling.

title: Blocking Redis inside the 15s price race: raw has_budget, flag-OFF provider gates, and per-200 record_usage steal race budget from every concurrent compare
evidence: Inside the race window a cold compare executes on-loop: has_budget('serper') raw (review_service.py:793 and :887 - unlike the spend gate these are NOT memoised; _redis_get at api_budget_service.py:376), _provider_gate_ok_async flag-OFF inline = is_circuit_closed + has_budget = 2xR per check per provider (scs:884, call sites scs:1423 firecrawl, scs:1497 scrapedo), and with a live key record_usage('serper') 1x incrby per 200 at ~10-15 calls/cold compare (serper_service.py:646,773,985,1077,1113,1154 -> api_budget_service.py:474). title: Post-response fire-and-forget tail blocks the loop ~0.9-1.6s per authed compare and is charged to OTHER users' latency
evidence: After the response returns, fire_and_forget schedules coroutines whose bodies are sync Supabase calls that run ON the loop: log_search (database_service.py:504), save_comparison_and_track_cohort = save_comparison + track_event insert (feedback_service.py:169) + Loop2 referral read sequentially (feedback_service.py:33-64), record_lifetime rpc (usage_service.py:277), and _update_behavior_profile's 4 sequential executes incl. a 50-row select and a JSONB update (scs:4288-4295, scheduled at scs:3431/4107). ~9xS = 0.9-1.1s warm (+L2 saves cold) that the submitting user never sees but every concurrent request queues behind. title: Ceiling note: Railway healthcheck shares the blocked loop - sustained saturation during a deploy window can flap the service
evidence: healthcheckPath /health, healthcheckTimeout 30, restartPolicyType ON_FAILURE maxRetries 3 (railway.json:8-11). /health itself is I/O-free (main.py:307-313) so it only fails when loop backlog exceeds 30s - which the model reaches past rho~1 (~N>=10-12 mixed-profile active users, or a >=15-user app-open burst). At that point the deploy probe times out, and with maxRetries 3 a redeploy during a traffic spike can loop restarts, each restart re-colding every in-process memo and the uvicorn startup (~10-20s cold start per CLAUDE.md), amplifying the outage. title: No client-side deadline on the SSE stream (or camera fetch) and abort is never invoked — backend's flag-OFF unbounded verdict tail can pin the loader forever
evidence: streamComparison's fetch (api.ts:410-413) has no timeout — the 120s axios timeout (api.ts:20) covers only the non-streaming fallback. On the STREAMING route the backend's STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS (30s, default 25 in code structured_comparison_service.py:1182) wraps only Phase 1; the post-Phase-1 verdict/critique/moderation tail is UNBOUNDED unless ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE is ON, which is default OFF and not flipped (CLAUDE.md M13-04/W3: 'flag OFF = today's unbounded tail'). M13-35's drain-not-abandon makes the server happily run that tail. HomeScreen stores the abort handle (HomeScreen.tsx:112, :313) but no code path ever CALLS abortRef.current — not on unmount, not on a cancel gesture (grep: set at 313, nulled at 324/352, never invoked) — so a stalled tail leaves the theatrical loader spinning indefinitely with no escape but force-close. identifyFromImages' raw fetch (api.ts:167-174) likewise has no timeout despite the '2 minutes for image processing' comment applying only to axios.
fix: Add a watchdog (e.g. 60s setTimeout calling controller.abort(), cleared on complete/error) inside streamComparison; call abortRef.current?.() in a HomeScreen unmount cleanup and from a loading-screen cancel affordance; wrap identifyFromImages' fetch with AbortController + timeout. Server-side the real fix is activating ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE (already a recorded M13-04 canary item).
verify_reason: The client-side facts check out: streamComparison's fetch (api.ts:410-413) passes only `signal`, no timeout, and the 120s axios timeout (api.ts:20) applies only to the fallback GET at :509; identifyFromImages' fetch (api.ts:167-174) likewise has no timeout; and `grep abortRef SmartCompareApp/src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx` returns exactly 4 hits - declared :112, assigned :313, nulled :324 and :352 - it is NEVER invoked, so there is no unmount cleanup and no cancel affordance. But the claimed failure ('pin the loader forever', 'spinning indefinitely') is overstated: the unbounded post-Phase-1 tail is still bounded per OpenAI call by openai_service.py:27/:53/:62 `httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=30.0)`, so the verdict/critique/moderation tail terminates and yields a complete or error event rather than hanging without end. What remains is a real hardening gap (a multi-minute loader with no user escape), not an infinite hang - P3. The backend half is M13-04/M13-35 as the finding itself states.

title: Unified error envelope drops tier/remaining from 429 USAGE_LIMIT — FE UsageLimitError type promises fields the wire never carries
evidence: text_routes packs detail={error, code:'USAGE_LIMIT', tier, remaining} (text_routes.py:175-183, same at :337-345/:488-496), but http_exception_handler (error_handler.py:75-100) rebuilds the body as exactly {success, error, code, request_id} — tier/remaining/reason are DROPPED on the wire. Today benign — PaywallScreen only uses initialUsage's truthiness to skip a fetch (PaywallScreen.tsx:216-225) — but the type is a standing lie: any future copy keyed on reason ('daily_limit' vs 'monthly_limit') or remaining will silently read undefined. Corollary: the legacy `data.detail.code` dual-reads (usageService.ts:62, api.ts:94/:188) are dead against this envelope — only the raw-fetch camera path could ever see a detail dict, and error_handler flattens that too.
fix: Either extend _build_error_response/http_exception_handler to pass through whitelisted structured-detail extras (tier, remaining, reason, layer) or mark UsageLimitError's fields optional and derive paywall copy from /usage/status instead. Pick one and delete the dead dual-read branch.
verify_reason: text_routes.py:175-183 raises HTTPException(429, detail={error, code:'USAGE_LIMIT', tier, remaining}); error_handler.py:74-100 http_exception_handler rebuilds the body as exactly {success, error, code, request_id} - tier and remaining are dropped on the wire, and `reason` was never in the detail dict at all (it is interpolated into the message string). usageService.ts:32-41 declares UsageLimitError.tier/reason/remaining as REQUIRED and getUsageLimitDetail (:71-74) casts the flattened payload straight into that type, so the type is a standing lie. Benign today because PaywallScreen only tests initialUsage for truthiness. P3 is the right severity.

title: parseApiError blankets every 503 to TIMEOUT, overriding explicit non-timeout codes like FEATURE_DISABLED

title: Phantom typed keys: scoring.win_margin and scoring.products never exist on the wire — share-CTA variants dead and invitee match score hardcoded to 78
evidence: Backend `scoring` block emits exactly {scores, dimension_winners, price_tiers, is_cross_tier, scoring_method, category_weights} (response_builder.py:1557-1564); win_margin lives ONLY at overview.winner.margin (:1429) and scoring_v2.win_margin. types.ts:348-349 declares ScoringResult.winner_index and .win_margin as required — both phantom. Consequences: (a) ResultsScreen.tsx:412 `const margin = scoring?.win_margin` is always undefined → ctaVariant is permanently 'default', so the F2.4 strong/close share-CTA variants never render (tsc can't catch it because the type asserts the field). (b) InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:156-160 reads `result?.scoring?.products ?? []` — no backend payload shape has scoring.products (real key: scoring.scores.product_N.overall) → rawScore always falls to the fallback and every invitee sees a fabricated '78' match score (compounded by run_invitee_quiz never actually re-scoring, referral_service.py:462-507, see MB-contract-05).
fix: Read win_margin from scoring_v2?.win_margin ?? overview?.winner?.margin in ResultsScreen; read the winner score via scoring.scores[`product_${idx}`]?.overall in InviteeQuizScreen; correct ScoringResult in types.ts to the six real keys so tsc regains teeth here.
verify_reason: response_builder.py:1557-1564 emits `scoring` with exactly six keys (scores, dimension_winners, price_tiers, is_cross_tier, scoring_method, category_weights) - no winner_index, no win_margin, no products. win_margin lives only at overview.winner.margin (:1429) and in scoring_v2. types.ts:348-349 declares ScoringResult.winner_index and .win_margin as REQUIRED, which is why tsc cannot flag ResultsScreen.tsx:412 `const margin = scoring?.win_margin` - always undefined, so :413 returns 'default' and the strong/close CTA variants are unreachable. InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:156 `result?.scoring?.products ?? []` then :160 `scoringProducts[winnerIdx]?.score ?? 78` - `scoring.products` exists in no backend shape (the real path is scoring.scores['product_N'].overall), so the 78 fallback is always taken (compounded by MB-contract-05 making that payload empty regardless). P3 correct.

title: History is hard-capped at 50 rows with no pagination and no truncation signal
evidence: loadHistory calls `getComparisonHistory(50, 0, searchQuery || undefined)` with literal limit/offset (HistoryScreen.tsx:356) and is the only call site; the SectionList has no onEndReached / onEndReachedThreshold and no footer loader (:790-804). The backend's `total` is stored (`setTotal(data.total || 0)`, :358) but rendered nowhere — its only other use is the decrement after a delete (:442). A user with more than 50 v2 comparisons therefore cannot reach comparison 51 by any means, is never told the list is partial, and the pull-to-refresh (:375-378) re-fetches the same first page.
fix: Append pages on onEndReached with an incrementing offset (guarded by `history.length < total`), or at minimum render the `total` so the truncation is visible.
verify_reason: Facts confirmed: HistoryScreen.tsx:356 is the only call site of getComparisonHistory and passes literal `(50, 0, searchQuery || undefined)` (the function's own defaults are 20/0, api.ts:216); the SectionList (:790-804) has no onEndReached/onEndReachedThreshold/ListFooterComponent — grep for onEndReached across SmartCompareApp/src returns nothing; `total` is stored at :358 and used only in the post-delete decrement at :442, never rendered. Downgraded from P2 because impact is bounded and entirely future-tense: nothing is lost or corrupted, the first page always loads, and reaching the cap requires 51+ saved v2 comparisons — not attainable under the current freemium caps and pre-activation usage. This is a known list-completeness gap, not a defect users hit today.

title: category_switched is never surfaced, so a user whose category hint was overridden is shown the result as if it matched their pick
evidence: The backend contract exists end to end except for the render: the flag is typed (`category_switched?: boolean`, src/types/types.ts:288) and the copy is present in BOTH catalogs (`results.categorySwitched` = 'Category adjusted to {{category}}' / 'الفئة عُدّلت إلى {{category}}'), but grep finds zero render sites — the banner was deleted in the S3 rewrite (ResultsScreen.tsx:721-724, `DELETE list executed: categorySwitchedBanner`). Meanwhile HomeScreen actively solicits the hint and tells the user it matters — `home.categories.nudge` = 'Pick a category for the most accurate compare' (HomeScreen.tsx:733-739) — and sends `selected_category` on both compare paths (:311, :413). So a user who deliberately picks Fragrances and receives a Skincare-schema comparison (different CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS weights, different spec schema, different fairness basis) is never told their choice was overridden, and the nudge that persuaded them to pick has no truthful counterpart in the result.
fix: Restore a non-banner disclosure honouring memory/feedback_no_info_banners.md — e.g. reflect the resolved category in the existing 'At a glance' section header, or show the chip in the resolved category's state on return — rather than leaving the flag, the type field and both translations orphaned.
verify_reason: The orphan is real: the backend computes and ships the flag (structured_comparison_service.py:282-319, response_builder.py:1070 and :1418 `"category_switched": category_switched`), the type field exists (types.ts:288), and both catalogs carry results.categorySwitched ('Category adjusted to {{category}}' / 'الفئة عُدّلت إلى {{category}}'), while a repo-wide grep finds no render site — the only other frontend mention is the deletion note itself (ResultsScreen.tsx:721-724). Downgraded from P2 because the omission is a recorded product decision, not an oversight: the delete list cites `memory/feedback_no_info_banners.md`, i.e. user feedback rejected info banners. What remains is dead type/copy surface plus an arguable disclosure gap against the home nudge (HomeScreen.tsx:732-739) — a design question to re-open, not a defect at P2.

title: Auth screens are the copy-contract hole: two catalog strings say 'failed' and every error path renders raw axios/backend English
evidence: A full scan of both catalogs for the forbidden vocab returns exactly two hits, both in auth: `auth.appleFailed` = 'Apple sign-in failed' and `auth.googleFailed` = 'Google sign-in failed' (ar.json is clean). Around them the screens render untranslated backend text: RegisterScreen falls back to the hardcoded `'Registration failed'` (RegisterScreen.tsx:211) and `result.error` itself is `error.response?.data?.detail || error.message || 'Registration failed'` (authService.ts:140, and :181 for login), so an offline signup shows the literal axios string 'Network Error' to an Arabic user. LoginScreen has the same precedence (`setError(result.error || t('auth.loginFailed'))`, LoginScreen.tsx:278) and all three screens render `parseApiError(err).message` in the catch (LoginScreen.tsx:209/226/281, RegisterScreen.tsx:214, ForgotPasswordScreen.tsx:52), which parseApiError deliberately returns as '' for TIMEOUT/503 (api.ts:635-637) — an empty red banner under the button.
fix: Rewrite the two catalog strings in the approved vocabulary, drop `result.error` from every user-facing setError in favour of a code-keyed t(), and branch on parseApiError().code so a TIMEOUT never renders an empty banner.
verify_reason: Partly right, and the headline symptom is wrong. Confirmed: the only 'failed' vocab in either catalog is en auth.appleFailed='Apple sign-in failed' and auth.googleFailed='Google sign-in failed' (ar renders both as 'لم يكتمل…'); authService.ts:140 and :181 return `error.response?.data?.detail || error.message || 'Registration failed'`, and RegisterScreen.tsx:211 / LoginScreen.tsx:205,232,278 render that value, so a bare axios 'Network Error' can reach an Arabic user. REFUTED sub-claim: parseApiError's `{message:'', code:'TIMEOUT'}` (api.ts:~635-637) does not produce 'an empty red banner' — both render sites are truthiness-guarded (`{error ? <View style={styles.errorBanner}>…</View> : null}`, LoginScreen.tsx:409-413, and the field text at :174), so the failure mode is a silent no-op instead. Downgraded to P3: the remaining substance is two English catalog strings and a copy-policy leak that is the same class M13-66 already files at HomeScreen.tsx:381, with the distinguishing evidence (the empty banner) not holding up.

title: ResultsScreen carries a write-only usageStatus plus a dead orchestrator helper block, costing a /usage/status round trip on every result view
evidence: `const [usageStatus, setUsageStatus] = useState<UsageStatus|null>(null)` (ResultsScreen.tsx:164) is populated by an unconditional `getUsageStatus().then(setUsageStatus)` on mount (:175-177) and read nowhere — grep for `usageStatus` across src/ returns only those two lines. So every Results open (including every history-row tap) fires an authenticated GET /api/v1/usage/status whose response is discarded. The same S3 rewrite left a block of orchestrator-local helpers unreferenced after rendering moved into ResultsContent: formatPrice (:394, superseded by the pending-aware copy at ResultsContent.tsx:122-135, so this one still returns the older 'Price N/A' for a pended price), getScoreColor (:403), getProductScores (:517), SCORE_LABELS (:532), priceDiff/getPriceDiff (:523,:541), filterSpecs/getAllSpecKeys/isSpecDifferent (:547-575), key_differences (:319) and the specsExpanded/showDiffsOnly state (:152,:154).
fix: Delete the usageStatus state and its fetch, and remove the dead helper block — keeping a second, stale formatPrice next to the live one invites a future edit to the wrong copy of the price-pending rule.
verify_reason: Both halves check out. `usageStatus` appears exactly twice in the whole of SmartCompareApp/src — the declaration at ResultsScreen.tsx:164 and the unconditional `useEffect(() => { getUsageStatus().then(setUsageStatus); }, [])` at :175-177 — so every Results open, including every history-row tap, fires an authenticated GET whose response is discarded. The helper block is likewise unreferenced after rendering moved to ResultsContent: formatPrice (:394), getScoreColor (:403), getProductScores (:517), getPriceDiff (:523) with priceDiff (:541), SCORE_LABELS (:532), filterSpecs (:547) / getAllSpecKeys (:558) / isSpecDifferent (:569), key_differences (:319) and the specsExpanded/showDiffsOnly state (:152, :154) — each name occurs only at its declaration plus the closed loop among themselves (filterSpecs from getAllSpecKeys, getPriceDiff from priceDiff). Outside M13-64's scope, which deleted whole zero-reference components rather than dead members inside a live screen. P3 is correct.

title: AR plural coverage is _one/_other only; Arabic counts 0,2,3-10,11-99 resolve to English, and both jest fences are structurally blind to it
evidence: ar.json:855-860 defines only expiresInDays/Hours/Minutes_one/_other, but CLDR Arabic has 6 plural categories. Runtime-proven with the app's own i18next@26 + catalogs (node, lng='ar', fallbackLng='en'): t('referrals.bonus.expiresInDays',{count}) => count 0/2/3/7/11 all return English 'Expires in N days'; only 1 and 100 return Arabic. Neither test can catch it: __tests__/i18n.test.ts:8-10 compares key SETS (EN can never carry _two/_few/_many, so AR lacking them is 'equal'), and the M13-15 fence __tests__/i18n/no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts:56-61 imports en.json only (line 25) and isPresent() passes if ANY one suffix exists — delete expiresInDays_other from BOTH catalogs and every i18n test stays green. Mitigating: zero src/ consumers today (grep 'expiresIn' hits only the catalogs — BonusCountdownCard was deleted in M13-64), so the 6-key family is currently dead weight that will leak English the day a countdown surface returns (referral system flag is ON in Railway).
fix: Add expiresIn*_zero/_two/_few/_many to ar.json (and _zero to en or accept en 2-form), then extend the fence: for every base key with any plural suffix, assert each catalog carries every category from new Intl.PluralRules(lng).resolvedOptions().pluralCategories — that single assertion makes the fence actually plural-aware. Alternatively delete the 6 dead keys until a consumer exists.
verify_reason: Evidence fully reproduced. ar.json:855-860 carries only _one/_other; Intl.PluralRules('ar').pluralCategories = zero,one,two,few,many,other; running the app's own i18next@26.1.0 over the real catalogs with lng='ar' returns 'Expires in 0/2/3/7/11 days' (English) and Arabic only for 1 and 100. Fence blindness re-derived at __tests__/i18n/no-missing-referenced-keys.test.ts:25 (imports en.json only) and :56-61 (isPresent() returns true if ANY one suffix exists), and __tests__/i18n.test.ts compares key SETS so AR can never be required to carry _two/_few/_many. Grepped docs/investigations/2026-08-31-m13-full-review.md for plural|PluralRules|_other|expiresIn: no M13 row covers plural categories, so this is NOT a re-file of M13-15 (which is about 65 absent keys). DOWNGRADED P2->P3 because I confirmed the finding's own mitigator: 'grep -rn expiresIn src/' returns zero hits — the 6-key family has no consumer at 593ec1e, so there is no user-visible English leak today. The defect is a latent dead-key + a real structural test gap, not a live Arabic regression.

title: No Intl.PluralRules polyfill and no compatibilityJSON: plural behavior on Hermes phones diverges from the Node/jest environment that validates it
evidence: src/i18n/index.ts:24-34 init has no compatibilityJSON and grep for 'intl-pluralrules|PluralRules|compatibilityJSON' across the app returns zero hits (package.json has no polyfill dep). i18next@26 resolves plural suffixes via new Intl.PluralRules (node_modules/i18next/dist/cjs/i18next.js:1060) and on throw silently degrades to dummyRule = {select: c => c===1 ? 'one' : 'other'} (:1032-1037,1068). Hermes' Intl subset has historically shipped without Intl.PluralRules, so device plural selection may be the crude one/other rule while jest (Node, full ICU) exercises real CLDR Arabic rules — tests validate behavior phones may not run, and MB-i18n-rtl-01's English leak flips on/off depending on which branch the runtime takes. Cannot be verified from this Windows box (two-lever model: phones run the last eas update bundle); re-derive on-device with console.log(typeof Intl.PluralRules) in a dev build.
fix: Add import 'intl-pluralrules' (the standard RN/i18next pairing) at the top of src/i18n/index.ts so device and jest resolve identical plural categories, and add a dev-build assertion/log that Intl.PluralRules exists.
verify_reason: Code facts all re-derived: src/i18n/index.ts:24-34 sets no compatibilityJSON; grep for 'intl-pluralrules|PluralRules|compatibilityJSON' across src/, App.tsx and package.json returns zero hits (no polyfill dep). node_modules/i18next/dist/cjs/i18next.js line numbers match exactly — dummyRule at :1032, 'new Intl.PluralRules' at :1060, and the silent degrade returns at :1066/:1068. So the divergence mechanism is real and the fix (import 'intl-pluralrules') is cheap and defensive. Caveat recorded rather than penalised because the finding states it honestly: the Hermes half is NOT verifiable from this box, and the stack is RN 0.81.5 / Expo ~54.0.33 where Hermes Intl coverage is much wider than in the era that made this the standard RN pairing — so the on-device divergence may well not occur. P3 is already the right ceiling given current impact is nil (rtl-01's keys are dead, rtl-08's keys have no plural forms at all so dummyRule vs real CLDR changes nothing there).

title: TwoInputShell double-mirrors under forceRTL: explicit 'row-reverse' when isRTL cancels RN's automatic row flip, putting the numeral circle on the wrong side in Arabic
evidence: TwoInputShell.tsx:684 'const rowDirection = isRTL ? "row-reverse" : "row"' applied at :687. The app force-enables native RTL (App.tsx:170-172, useLanguage.ts:17-19), and under I18nManager.isRTL=true RN/Yoga already lays flexDirection:'row' out right-to-left — so 'row-reverse' in an RTL container yields visual LTR: the numeral circle (first child, :688) lands on the LEFT of the box in Arabic, the exact opposite of the component's own spec comment at :116-117 ('numeral circle sits on the right of the box in AR'). The RTL tests (src/components/__tests__/TwoInputShell.test.tsx:892+) pin the style literal flexDirection==='row-reverse' against a react-native __mock__ with no Yoga layout, so they encode the bug rather than the visual. The manually-swapped hairlineLTR/RTL edge styles (:114-115) are at risk of the same double-swap depending on RN's left/right-swap-in-RTL default. This is the primary Home compare input pair.
fix: Under forceRTL, keep flexDirection:'row' in both directions and delete the manual LTR/RTL edge-style forks (native RTL handles them), OR verify on an Arabic device/EAS build and pin a layout-level (not style-literal) assertion. Decide once whether the app's RTL strategy is native-flip or manual-flip — today it mixes both.
verify_reason: Code is exactly as cited: TwoInputShell.tsx:284 'const isRTL = I18nManager.isRTL', :684 rowDirection = isRTL ? 'row-reverse' : 'row', applied at :687 over styles.row (:806-809, which sets no flexDirection of its own), with the circle as first child at :688; the spec comment at :116-117 does say the numeral circle should sit on the RIGHT in AR; and native RTL is force-enabled (App.tsx:170-172). The Yoga argument is sound in principle — under direction:RTL a 'row' already lays out right-to-left, so 'row-reverse' returns it to visual LTR and contradicts the component's own spec. DOWNGRADED P2->P3 because the harmful half is an un-run layout inference: I cannot execute RN layout from this box, the tests the finding itself criticises (TwoInputShell.test.tsx:892+) only pin the style literal against a Yoga-less mock, and the hairlineLTR/RTL half is explicitly hedged ('at risk of'). What is certainly true and worth fixing — code contradicting its own documented spec, an RTL strategy that mixes native-flip and manual-flip, and a test that encodes a literal instead of a layout — is a P3-grade consistency defect, not a confirmed P2 visual break.

title: Five physical textAlign:'left'/'right' sites are not RTL-aware; the ResultsAccordion spec-value cells invert their hug-the-center design in Arabic
evidence: RN textAlign 'left'/'right' is physical (the codebase itself knows this: InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:500 correctly writes textAlign: I18nManager.isRTL ? 'left' : 'right'). Unhandled sites: ResultsAccordion.tsx:880 specsCellValueLeft textAlign:'right' ('hugs the centered label') and :884 specsCellValueRight textAlign:'left' — in RTL the row order flips but the alignments stay physical, so both product spec values push to the OUTER screen edges leaving gaps beside the centered label, inverting the documented design (:878-882 comments); ContactUsScreen.tsx:278 charCount textAlign:'right' (stays bottom-right in AR where the natural position is bottom-left); ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:617 prioritiesPercent; DimensionBars.tsx:452 legendNameRight. Re-derive: grep -rn "textAlign: '(left|right)'" src.
fix: Make each site direction-conditional like InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:500, or restructure the accordion cells to justify content toward the label with flex alignment instead of textAlign.
verify_reason: 'grep -rn "textAlign: .left.|textAlign: .right." src/' returns exactly the five cited sites and no others: ResultsAccordion.tsx:880 ('right') and :884 ('left'), ContactUsScreen.tsx:278, ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:617, DimensionBars.tsx:452. The counterexample proving the codebase knows the difference is confirmed verbatim at InviteeQuizScreen.tsx:500 — 'textAlign: I18nManager.isRTL ? "left" : "right"' with a comment explaining the trailing-edge intent. RN textAlign left/right is physical while the surrounding rows flip, so the accordion's centre-hugging design does invert. P3 is correctly calibrated: cosmetic alignment drift, no functional loss.

title: Arabic-Indic digit policy is inconsistent across ar.json (32 values Arabic-Indic vs 20 Western), including the same sentence in both systems and one string mixing both
evidence: Scripted count over ar.json: 32 values use Arabic-Indic digits, 20 use Western. Direct contradictions: identical EN copy 'Qaren cross-checks 25+ retailers' ships as '25' at ar.json:179 (loading.tip.cross_checks) and '٢٥' at ar.json:626 (results.tips.retailers) — loading screen and results screen, seconds apart; '70 comparisons per month' is '٧٠' at ar.json:255 (paywall.features.unlimited) and '70' at ar.json:898 (paywall.features.comparisons); 'اختر حتى ٣' (onboarding.s8.subtitle) vs 'اختر حتى 3' (preferences.priorities.helper). Mixed within ONE string: ar.json:883 home.camera.slotIndicator '{{index}} من ٢' — ScanCameraScreen.tsx:343-349 (W4-touched, M13-15 key) interpolates a JS number so the pill renders '1 من ٢' (Western 1, Arabic-Indic ٢), while the sibling a11y key home.camera.a11y.slot uses Western '2'. src/utils/formatDate.ts:4-5 declares ASCII-in-interpolations as 'the rest of the app's idiom' yet its own formatDate(...,'ar') emits Arabic-Indic (Node-verified: '١ أغسطس').
fix: Pick one policy (the formatDate comment says ASCII), normalize the 32-vs-20 split in ar.json to it, fix slotIndicator's hardcoded ٢, and add a jest fence rejecting [٠-٩] (or [0-9], per the chosen policy) in ar.json values.
verify_reason: Scripted the ar.json scan myself: 32 values contain Arabic-Indic [٠-٩], 20 contain Western [0-9] after stripping {{...}} interpolations — the 32/20 split is exact. All four contradiction pairs reproduce verbatim: loading.tip.cross_checks '...أكثر من 25 متجراً' vs results.tips.retailers '...أكثر من ٢٥ متجراً' (same EN source string 'Qaren cross-checks 25+ retailers'); paywall.features.unlimited '٧٠ مقارنة شهرياً' vs paywall.features.comparisons '70 مقارنة شهرياً' (same EN); onboarding.s8.subtitle 'اختر حتى ٣' vs preferences.priorities.helper 'اختر حتى 3' (both EN 'Pick up to 3'). home.camera.slotIndicator = '{{index}} من ٢' with ScanCameraScreen.tsx:341-343 interpolating a JS number, so the pill really does render Western index + Arabic-Indic ٢, while the sibling home.camera.a11y.slot uses Western '2'. formatDate.ts:4-5 does declare the ASCII idiom while node confirms its own ar-SA path emits '١ أغسطس'. Distinct from open M13-69, which is about CALL-SITE locale drift; this row is catalog values. The M13-69 correction is also right and independently verified: Intl.DateTimeFormat('ar-SA').resolvedOptions().calendar === 'gregory', so M13-69's Hijri headline is wrong and its real effect is Arabic-Indic digits.

title: Currency display is two different languages in one app: Results shows Latin ISO codes with unpinned toLocaleString, Paywall shows localized 'د.ب' — and BHD loses its 3-decimal convention
evidence: ResultsContent.tsx:129 and ResultsScreen.tsx:396 render prices as `${price.currency} ${price.amount.toLocaleString()}`: (a) the ISO code stays Latin 'BHD'/'SAR'/'AED' in the Arabic UI while the Paywall hardcodes localized symbols — ar.json:900 paywall.plan.monthly_price '2.9 د.ب' (EN twin en.json:903 '2.9 BHD'); (b) toLocaleString() has NO locale argument, so digits/separators follow DEVICE locale, not app language — Node-verified (1234.5).toLocaleString('ar-SA') = '١٬٢٣٤٫٥', i.e. an ar-region device shows Arabic-Indic prices inside the English UI and vice versa — while LoadingRings.tsx:58 and StatBlock.tsx:29 pin 'en-US' for their numbers, so one screen can mix digit systems; (c) BHD is a 3-minor-unit currency: 77.000 renders 'BHD 77' and 12.5 'BHD 12.5', never the conventional '77.000'. Note also symbol-order: Paywall reads amount-then-symbol, Results code-then-amount.
fix: One shared formatMoney(amount, currency, appLanguage) using Intl.NumberFormat(appLocale, {style:'currency', currency}) (gives د.ب.‏ in ar, 3 decimals for BHD automatically) or, minimally, pin the locale to the app language and add an i18n key per currency code.
verify_reason: Scope reduced to sub-claim (a) only; (b) and (c) are re-files of open M13-69 and are refuted as duplicates. Verified code: ResultsContent.tsx:129 and ResultsScreen.tsx:396 both build `${price.currency} ${price.amount.toLocaleString()}`, and node confirms (1234.5).toLocaleString('ar-SA') = '١٬٢٣٤٫٥' and (77).toLocaleString() = '77'. But M13-69 in docs/investigations/2026-08-31-m13-full-review.md:98 already states 'prices use device-locale digits inconsistently' and prescribes, verbatim, 'give every toLocaleString call the same explicit locale plus minimumFractionDigits via one shared money formatter' — that is exactly sub-claim (b) and the BHD 3-minor-unit fix in (c), so both are already-filed work. Only (a) survives as new: paywall.plan.monthly_price ships '2.9 د.ب' in AR (en.json twin '2.9 BHD') while Results renders the Latin ISO code inside the Arabic UI, plus the amount-then-symbol vs code-then-amount order flip. That residue is genuine but cosmetic — P3.

title: Live {count} call sites resolve to bare keys with no plural forms — 'Across 1 decisions' / 'عبر 1 قرارات' at count=1
evidence: The only three live t(key,{count}) sites (HomeEditorialSections.tsx:296 home.savings.count; ImageSlotRow.tsx:37 home.camera.a11y.slot; ShareBottomSheet.tsx:318 referrals.share.maxReached) all reference keys that exist ONLY as bare keys — no _one/_other in either catalog (en.json:29/ar.json:24 etc.). i18next falls back from key_other to the bare key, so all counts share one string: runtime-proven t('home.savings.count',{count:1}) => 'عبر 1 قرارات نظّمتها مع قارن.' (and EN 'Across 1 decisions...') — wrong singular grammar in both languages for a real new-user state (stats.decisions_count===1). maxReached is effectively constant (LIFETIME_CAP) and slot count∈{1,2} reads acceptably, so savings.count is the visible case.
fix: Add home.savings.count_one/_other (EN) + the Arabic category set per MB-i18n-rtl-01's fence extension; grammar for the other two keys is optional polish.
verify_reason: Runtime-reproduced with the app's own i18next and catalogs: t('home.savings.count',{count:1}) returns 'عبر 1 قرارات نظّمتها مع قارن.' in ar and 'Across 1 decisions sorted with Qaren.' in en — i18next falls back from key_other to the bare key, so singular grammar is wrong in BOTH languages. The three live count call sites are exactly the three claimed and no others ('grep count: src/ | grep t('): HomeEditorialSections.tsx:296 (home.savings.count, fed by stats.decisions_count so count===1 is a real new-user state), ImageSlotRow.tsx:37, ShareBottomSheet.tsx:318. Neither catalog carries _one/_other for any of the three. The finding's own triage is honest — maxReached is pinned to LIFETIME_CAP and slot count is 1..2, leaving savings.count as the single visible case. This is the lane's one LIVE plural defect (rtl-01's keys are dead), and P3 is right for a grammar/polish issue.

title: W4's new ScanCameraScreen permission pad ignores the arabicLineHeightMultiplier contract — which only 2 components app-wide actually consume
evidence: The design contract (theme/index.ts:102 arabicLineHeightMultiplier = 1.7/1.5; CLAUDE.md 'arabicLineHeightMultiplier = 1.7/1.5') is consumed by exactly two components: grep -rln arabicLineHeight src => PaywallBanner.tsx, TwoInputShell.tsx (+ theme). The Wave-4 permission pad added by commit 58ef1d1 (M13-54) renders new multi-line Arabic copy with unadjusted EN line heights: ScanCameraScreen.tsx:622-628 permissionTitle spreads typography.title and :629-635 permissionText spreads typography.body (fontSize*1.5 per theme/index.ts:94-98) with no AR branch — on the dark camera surface where Cairo's taller ascenders/diacritics are clip-prone. Note two-lever model: this W4 code is on main but not yet on phones until eas update.

title: Pre-SecureStore plaintext token residue in AsyncStorage is never deleted, and Android auto-backup includes it
evidence: Until commit 0475d85 (2026-04-04, 'security: migrate tokens from AsyncStorage to expo-secure-store') access AND refresh tokens were written to AsyncStorage under '@qaren_token'/'@qaren_refresh_token' (and '@smartcompare_token'/'@smartcompare_refresh_token' before rename 701f501, 2026-03-28). The migration diff shows every read/write switched to SecureStore and the old `AsyncStorage.multiRemove([USER, TOKEN, REFRESH])` in clearSession replaced by SecureStore deletes — but NO removal of the legacy AsyncStorage keys was ever added: grep for 'qaren_token|qaren_refresh|smartcompare_token|multiRemove' across src matches only the SecureStore constants (authService.ts:67-68, note current SecureStore keys have no '@' so they cannot alias the old keys). A device that logged in on a pre-Apr-2026 build carries a plaintext Supabase REFRESH token in AsyncStorage forever; if the app was abandoned before the migration, that token was never rotated and may still be valid (Supabase refresh tokens invalidate on use, not by age). app.json sets no android.allowBackup (grep confirms), so Expo's default `true` makes the plaintext RKStorage database eligible for Google Drive auto-backup, while SecureStore values are Keystore-bound and effectively excluded — the residue is strictly weaker than the live store.
fix: One-time hygiene sweep at app boot (e.g., in initializeAuth): `AsyncStorage.multiRemove(['@qaren_token','@qaren_refresh_token','@smartcompare_token','@smartcompare_refresh_token'])`, fire-and-forget. Optionally set android.allowBackup:false (or a fullBackupContent exclusion for RKStorage) in app.json — note that half requires an `eas build`, the multiRemove ships via `eas update`.

Downgraded P2->P3: the exposed population is permanently capped at devices that logged in on pre-Apr-2026 internal-tester builds (<10 testers, app never publicly launched — new installs never have residue), and on any device that kept using the app the residual refresh token was consumed by Supabase rotation; the live-token scenario requires abandonment before the migration ever ran. title: Google sign-in has no nonce binding (Supabase 'Skip nonce checks' ON) — any bearer of a valid Google id_token can mint a Qaren session
evidence: authService.ts:489-497 documents the B4 resolution: @react-native-google-signin embeds a HASHED nonce in the id_token without exposing the raw value, the FE can never satisfy Supabase's SHA-256(raw)==claim parity, so the server-side 'Skip nonce checks' toggle is ON and the request body is exactly {provider, id_token} (:497). Contrast the Apple path, which does full raw-nonce/SHA-256 binding via expo-crypto (:577-591). Residual risk: an id_token exfiltrated anywhere (device log, proxy on an unpinned dev build, Google-side leak) is replayable against /auth/social-login for its full TTL (~1h) with no client binding; protection rests solely on Google's signature, the aud check, and TTL. This is a deliberate, documented library-forced tradeoff — filed as an accepted-risk record so it is revisited rather than rediscovered.
fix: Track upstream: adopt raw-nonce support if @react-native-google-signin exposes it, or migrate Google auth to an Authorization-Code+PKCE flow (expo-auth-session) which removes the replayable-bearer-token shape entirely; until then keep the diagnostic Sentry captures and certificate pinning as compensating controls.
verify_reason: Evidence verified verbatim: authService.ts:489-497 documents the B4 resolution (library embeds a hashed nonce without exposing the raw value, Supabase 'Skip nonce checks' ON, request body exactly {provider, id_token}), while the Apple path at :576-591 does full raw-nonce/SHA-256 binding via expo-crypto — confirming the asymmetry is library-forced, not oversight. title: Release-build pinning init failure is silent fail-open — the catch assumes Expo Go and emits no production telemetry
