title: Winner axis is the weakest judged axis and flips on identical queries within hours
evidence: eval_runs: winner axis 0.36 on the full-200 (4aee8e88), 0.40/0.50 on the two smoke20 runs — the lowest of the four axes while carrying the heaviest gold weight (0.30). Recorded corroboration: gold elec-001 ('iPhone 15 vs Galaxy S24', ratified winner 0) was recorded 3x on 2026-05-05: eaf479bb 03:06 winner=1 (Galaxy 350 BHD, ratings 4.7/4.7), 4b4ad16a 03:08 winner=0 (Galaxy price flipped to 399), 6ff5f5b4 18:57 winner=1 (Galaxy back to 350; iPhone rating flipped 4.7→3.5) — the winner tracked transient price/rating capture variance, and 2 of 3 shipped outputs contradict the ratified winner. The product's core promise (the winner verdict) is its least reliable output.
fix: Add hysteresis for near-ties (win_margin below a threshold → present as 'close call' instead of a hard winner), pin rating provenance so a run-to-run source change cannot flip the verdict, and prioritize the winner axis in the next eval-gated fix wave (it is the heaviest-weighted axis at the lowest score).
verify_reason: No current-code defect re-derived; this is a June-era eval observation plus May-era recorded rows, exactly what the lane context says to discount. The cited anchor scoring_service.py:809 is `reasons.append('leads on the overall picture')` inside `build_winner_evidence` — unrelated to winner selection. The three elec-001 rows are dated 2026-05-05, before the fragrance-capture merge, wave-3 hardening and all four M13 waves; the axis numbers are from 2026-06-10/17. The 'no hysteresis' sub-claim is real but is a deliberate, documented invariant, not an oversight: _build_scoring_v2 (response_builder.py:956-971) explicitly FORCES argmax separation on a calibrated tie (nudging the loser, or raising the winner at the calibration floor) because the FE derives the winner from `product_a >= product_b`. Presenting near-ties as 'close call' is a product decision worth taking, but it is a roadmap item, not a P1 defect.

title: 18/26 recorded outputs shipped under category 'other', producing all-N/A generic spec tables
evidence: category_used='other' in 18/26 rows, including blatant electronics ('iphone 17 pro max vs Galaxy S25 ultra' 1c442680/2bf16403, 'Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra 256GB vs Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB' dddc1d6b, 'Glorious Model O Gaming Mouse vs Ducky One 2 …' f765e343) and all six text-input TOM FORD fragrance compares. Consequence chain in the same rows: the generic 7-field 'other' schema shipped with 100% 'N/A' values in 9 rows (e.g. 8c19fe72 both products color/origin/weight/features/material/warranty/dimensions all 'N/A') and ≥25% N/A in 19/26; scoring ran generic dims instead of CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS. The deterministic classifier (classify_category_from_text, :1108-1131) still returns 'other' TODAY for 'iphone 17 pro max Galaxy S25 ultra' and 'Gaming Mouse … Mechanical Keyboard' (verified offline), so with OpenAI degraded (as now) both the parser path and the A2b escalation fail back to 'other' and reproduce this. These rows also stay user-visible forever via History.
fix: Add the obvious high-traffic tokens (iphone, galaxy, phone models, mouse, keyboard, laptop-class words already partially present) to _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS so the $0 classifier catches mainstream electronics without the LLM; add a category-correctness assertion to the eval (gold rows carry category) so 'other'-collapse is measured per run.
verify_reason: The offline half reproduces — I ran classify_category_from_text at 593ec1e and it returns 'other' for 'iphone 17 pro max vs Galaxy S25 ultra', the mouse/keyboard pair, and the TOM FORD pair ('mouse'/'keyboard'/'iphone' are absent from _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS; only 'phone'/'smartphone' are present, and they need a word boundary). But the mechanism and the proposed fix are wrong for the dominant subset. extraction_service.py:1108-1120 documents the 'other' return as a deliberate policy ('We do NOT widen the synonym map with brand names (brittle, unbounded)'), and structured_comparison_service.py:_resolve_pair_category:290-308 shows that on the parser (q=/text) path — which is all six TOM FORD text compares — `det = llm_cat` only; classify_category_from_text is never consulted and A2b is deliberately not re-invoked. Widening _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS would be a no-op there. The all-N/A spec-table consequence is asserted from June payloads and not re-derived against current code. The eval category-assertion suggestion is the one durable part.

title: Two scoring systems ship in one payload; winner-card margin comes from the legacy one
evidence: Row 9a24786f: overview.winner.margin=7.8 and winner_reason 'scores 7.8 points higher…' derive from legacy products.overall_score (49.8/57.6), while scoring_v2.overall_score shows 70/74 with win_margin=4 — the score bars the UI renders. 4/26 rows have this material disagreement (9a24786f 7.8-vs-4, 2a5d828d 24.4-vs-12, 6807ce77 20.1-vs-10, 8c19fe72 5.1-vs-2); in every case the prose matches the legacy margin, proving the verdict text is generated off v1 numbers the user never sees.
fix: Make scoring_v2 the single numeric source for margin + verdict-prompt input; stop emitting legacy overall_score/scoring.scores into the payload (or rename them _debug) so prose generation cannot bind to them.
verify_reason: Not 'two scoring systems' — one system at two scales. `overview.winner.margin` is the raw `scoring_result['win_margin']` (response_builder.py:1148, :1429) while `scoring_v2.win_margin` is `abs(calibrate_score(a) - calibrate_score(b))` (:936-937, :1002), and calibrate_score is the linear `70 + (raw-50)*0.5`, which is exactly why every cited pair is 2:1 (7.8/4, 24.4/12, 20.1/10, 5.1/2). The user-visible half is gone: grep of SmartCompareApp/src finds no consumer of `overview.winner.margin` at all (the only margin read is ResultsScreen.tsx:412 `scoring?.win_margin`, feeding a CTA copy variant, not a displayed number), and the 'scores 7.8 points higher' prose is dropped wholesale by the `\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*points?\b` pattern in strip_score_internals — I verified it returns only the surviving sentence. Residual value: the dual-scale emission is a real trap for a future consumer.

title: Review summaries assert volume/agreement with zero verified reviews and launder marketing copy as owner consensus
evidence: Rows 9a24786f and 779200c0 ship review_summary.review_volume='moderate'/'high' + agreement_level='moderate'/'strong' while the same payload's scoring_v2.confidence_details.reviews = {review_count: 0, verified: false, source: null}. The praise line (:429-439) mechanically prefixes 'Owners consistently highlight ' to whatever highlight clause survives — in 9a24786f that clause is Tom Ford ad copy ('…redefines oud with luminous floral depth, featuring richness from geranium absolute and living red peony'), so brand marketing renders as owner consensus. 4/26 rows total flagged on volume/verification contradictions.
fix: Gate review_volume/agreement_level emission on a nonzero verified review_count (omit the fields otherwise), and suppress the 'Owners consistently highlight' framing when the source snippets came from vendor/brand domains (the snippet domain is already known at citation-cleaning time).
verify_reason: The volume/agreement half is dormant, not shipped copy: review_volume/agreement_level are GPT-extracted with `setdefault` fallbacks (extraction_service.py:1664-1665, response_builder.py:1531-1532) and grep of SmartCompareApp/src finds them only in types.ts:234-235 — ResultsAccordion.tsx:333-338 documents that the `review_summary.highlights` rendering was REMOVED under Contract 2, so nothing paints 'moderate volume / strong agreement'. The praise half is live but weaker than filed: review_service.py:_frame_praise_clause (:421-439) picks among four glues by grammatical shape — 'Owners consistently highlight' is the noun-phrase-lead fallback, not a mechanical prefix — and build_review_praise (:506+) applies de-attribution plus a copy-policy banned-vocab scrub. There is genuinely no source-domain gate, so vendor prose can still be framed as owner sentiment, but that is an LLM-input-quality risk evidenced only from pre-2026-06-21 payloads (review_praise itself only landed 2026-06-17 f6f198d/830089f) and not re-derived against current code.

title: Fact-check computes damning signals that never reach the shipped price/review confidence
evidence: 17/26 rows: fact_check specs_verified=0 (with 7-18 unverified citations); 14/26 rows: price_deviation_pct >30% vs the Shopping median (up to 85.4% — 11651c1d 84.9%, ad562ca4 85.4%, 9a24786f 52.9%). In the same payloads the shipped price object still carries confidence 0.95, review agreement 'strong', and metadata.comparison_quality='normal'. overview.confidence.overall does say 'low' (the one place it propagates), but the contradictory per-field confidences ship anyway — an internally inconsistent honesty story (price confidence 0.95 + price_verified false + 52.9% deviation in one response).
fix: Propagate fact-check outcomes into the fields users/clients actually read: cap price.confidence when price_verified is false and deviation_pct >30, and downgrade review agreement claims when specs_verified==0/review verification failed.
verify_reason: 'Never reach' is wrong. scoring_service.py:1446-1464 consumes the fact-check buckets as the trust dimension score, adding +0.1 when `price_verified` is true and -0.1 when review sentiment is inconsistent, and returning None (so MISSING_SCORE propagation fires) when no bucket is populated. fact_check_service.py:212-233 `is_data_freshness_shaky` consumes price_verified/specs/sentiment for the inline notice, and the finding itself concedes `overview.confidence.overall` reports 'low'. The remaining claim compares unlike things: `price.confidence` (0.95) is a CAPTURE confidence produced by the extractor's source_method, not agreement with a Shopping median — capping it on deviation would conflate two signals, and the front-door gate M13-W1 shipped (`is_price_showable(..., enforce_correctness=True)`, response_builder.py:1268) is the mechanism that actually pends a bad price. Review 'agreement strong' is not rendered (see PO-recorded-07). Evidence is entirely mid-June recorded payloads.

verify_reason: The arithmetic checks out — eval_runner.py:856-862 `grade_factual` is boolean per query, so axis_avg_factual 0.77 on a 200-query run does imply ~46 queries carried a gold-listed forbidden substring — but this is a restatement of one number from a 2026-06-10 eval row, not a defect with a failing code path. The cited anchor scripts/eval_runner.py:856 is the grader's own definition, not a bug site, and the fix ('run the full-200 when credits return, then look at metadata.failing_ids') is the same action already filed as PO-recorded-12 and already NEXT in the plan. title: Doubled-brand display strings ship in winner declarations and evidence lines
evidence: User-visible doubled brands in recorded payloads: winner declaration 'TOM FORD TOM FORD SOLEIL NEIGE 100ML' (779200c0), winner_evidence 'TOM FORD TOM FORD OUD WOOD 100 ML leads on the overall picture' (9a24786f, string assembled at scoring_service.py:809), product_names 'Louis Vuitton Louis Vuitton LV Vers Mesh Cap' (8c115710/1390cedf), 'HealthAid HealthAid Vitamin D3 1000 IU' (894d1926). Root: full_name = f"{brand} {name}" (openai_service.py:271, 342; same pattern price_service.py:837) without checking whether name already starts with brand.
fix: One shared helper: full_name = name if name.lower().startswith(brand.lower()) else f"{brand} {name}" — apply at the three construction sites.
verify_reason: The defect is real but the primary citation is wrong. openai_service.py:271 and :342 build `full_name` purely as PROMPT text ('Extract these specific fields for {full_name} from the snippets below' / 'Synthesize these specific fields for {full_name}'), and price_service.py:837 is Gate 0's length/first-char validator — none of the three is a display string, so none can be the root of a user-visible doubled brand. The genuine site is scoring_service.py:761-764 `_product_name_for_evidence`, `f"{p.get('brand','')} {p.get('name','')}".strip()` with no startswith check, consumed at :815-816 to build the winner_evidence lines that scoring_v2.winner_evidence ships — which is exactly the finding's 'TOM FORD TOM FORD OUD WOOD 100 ML leads on the overall picture' example (the trailing clause is the :818 fallback reason). The declaration and product_names examples come from GPT extraction emitting a brand-prefixed `name`, which no concat helper can fix. P3 is correct (cosmetic); apply the guard at scoring_service.py:762, not at the three cited sites.

title: Session +/-5% signals shift positionally-guessed dims - 'reviews' dwell boosts build quality in electronics
evidence: apply_session_signals maps tabs by POSITION: specs->dim_keys[0], reviews->dim_keys[2], overview->dim_keys[3] 'as price/value proxy' (lines 2207-2214). Against CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS order + _DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP: electronics reviews-dwell boosts build_quality_score (a reliability/fact-check signal; the actual review dim is futureproof_score at index 5) and overview boosts feature_score (not a value dim); fragrances overview-dwell boosts versatility_score (reliability). So the one behavioral layer that DOES key-match (unlike PO-rubric-05) systematically nudges the wrong dims in most categories. Impact bounded by the 5% cap; currently latent on the live path (no session_signals= caller in structured_comparison_service - grep shows compute_scores called with preferences/behavior_profile/cohort_profile only), but any wiring of compute_session_signals activates the wrong mapping silently.
fix: Replace positional guesses with a _DIMENSION_SIGNAL_MAP lookup: specs->the category's 'spec' dim, reviews->its 'review' dim, overview->its 'value' dim.
verify_reason: Reproduced: apply_session_signals maps tabs positionally (scoring_service.py:2209-2214 — dim_keys[0]/[2]/[3]). Probe on electronics with dominant reviews-dwell: build_quality_score (+0.0076, a reliability/fact-check dim) is the largest gainer while the actual review dim futureproof_score moves only +0.0018 via renormalization spillover; overview maps to feature_score (spec_secondary), not the value dim. Latent confirmed: grep of structured_comparison_service shows compute_scores called only with preferences/behavior_profile/cohort_profile — no session_signals caller. Bounded by the 5% cap. Not in M13. P3 appropriate.

title: Value-math gap (35 xfail stubs): a budget-tier user comparing two luxury products gets zero acknowledgment anywhere
evidence: The module-level xfail (line 63) maps the unshipped A.6.x surface exactly: _classify_value_match + build_value_match_caption (product tier vs user budget -> 'Above your usual range' captions, lines 226-296), _classify_budget_mismatch + the budget_mismatch kwarg on _build_preferences_prompt (verdict-prompt context when BOTH products sit outside the user's stated budget, lines 303-358), and richer delta_text ('40% less' / '0.9 stars higher', lines 175-218). User-visible cost today: (a) a user who stated budget='budget' comparing two luxury fragrances gets a verdict that reasons as if the products are in range - the CATEGORY_BUDGET_ADJUSTMENTS weight shift applies (+/-30% layer works) but no caption, no prompt context, no tier framing except the generic cross-tier note; (b) price deltas render only as absolute currency ('BHD 3.76 less', _dim_price line 2481) with no relative anchor; (c) 11 of the 35 stubs pin DIFFERENT coefficients than the shipped VALUE_FORMULA_BY_PRIORITY (spec 0.40/0.60 price row vs shipped 0.45/0.55 etc.) - the S3 v2 'value = value-for-money' re-tune (lines 532-549) deliberately superseded spec section 4a, so the stub table is stale against a ratified later decision and will assert wrong numbers the day someone 'fixes' them to green.
fix: Two-part: (1) implement _classify_value_match/_classify_budget_mismatch + captions (the budget-mismatch invisibility is the real product gap), and (2) re-ratify the C.5.1 coefficient table against the shipped S3-v2 values BEFORE un-xfailing, updating EXPECTED_COEFFICIENTS to the current ratified rows so the stubs don't revert the cheaper-bias fix.
verify_reason: All three legs verified. (a) The A.6.x surface is genuinely unshipped: _classify_value_match, _classify_budget_mismatch, build_value_match_caption, build_value_delta_text have zero hits in app/, and _build_preferences_prompt (extraction_service.py:1686-1689) takes no budget_mismatch kwarg — so a budget user comparing two luxury products gets the weight shift (CATEGORY_BUDget_ADJUSTMENTS applies at scoring_service.py:1216-1221) but no caption or prompt context. (b) Price deltas render absolute only: scoring_service.py:2481 `f"{currency} {diff:g} less"` in _dim_price — citation exact. (c) Coefficient staleness confirmed: EXPECTED_COEFFICIENTS (test_value_math.py:78-87) pins price 0.40/0.60, _default 0.60/0.40 vs the shipped S3-v2 deliberate re-tune 0.45/0.55 and 0.70/0.30 (scoring_service.py:533-549); the test file's own comment (lines 49-56) records 11 AssertionError nodes pinning pre-v1.1 numbers, so un-xfailing without re-ratification would revert the cheaper-bias fix. Not an M13 duplicate: M13-122 covers only the xfail reason's CLAUDE.md line-number drift and M13-80 covers the adjacent test_personalization_bundle_c.py stubs. P3 appropriate.

title: The documented +/-30% explicit cap drifts to +32% after renormalization
evidence: _compute_weights clamps each dim to +/-30% of its category weight (lines 1224-1228) but then renormalizes ONCE (lines 1231-1233) without re-checking, unlike _apply_capped_adjustments' 3-iteration cap-then-renormalize loop (lines 2116-2130) used by the behavioral/session/cohort paths. Probe: preferences {priorities:['price'], budget:'budget'} on electronics yields value_score +32.0% vs the category default (cap doc: 30%). Small (2pp) but it means the one cap that is user-facing marketing ('explicit +/-30%', CLAUDE.md + skill doc) is the one path that does not enforce it, and the drift grows with the number of down-shifted dims.
fix: Route the explicit path through the same _apply_capped_adjustments iterate-and-recheck helper the other three layers already use (pass max_ratio=MAX_WEIGHT_SHIFT_RATIO).
verify_reason: Reproduced: _compute_weights({'priorities':['price'],'budget':'budget'}, 'electronics') yields value_score 0.2640 vs the 0.20 category default = +32.0% against the documented +/-30% cap. Mechanism verified: lines 1224-1228 clamp per-dim, then lines 1231-1233 renormalize ONCE with no recheck, unlike _apply_capped_adjustments' 3-iteration cap-then-renormalize loop (lines 2116-2130) used by the behavioral/session/cohort layers. Arithmetic re-derived independently (0.26/0.985 = 0.2640). Small drift (2pp) on the one user-facing documented cap; not in M13. P3 appropriate.

title: Never-empty-cons prompt rule converts pipeline data gaps into product criticism — degraded tiers dress emptiness as flaws
evidence: Recorded cons across 6 rows: 'Limited detailed specs available', 'No specific material or origin information', 'Limited information on specific scent notes', 'Lacks comprehensive review data', 'Limited information on longevity', and the self-parodying 'No specific cons noted in reviews' (row 9045ffb1). COMPARISON_SYSTEM:982 orders 'NEVER return empty pros[] or cons[] arrays — every product has SOME observable strengths and weaknesses', so under thin specs/reviews (the modal degraded tier) the model fabricates meta-cons that blame the product for OUR missing data — misleading and unfair to the runner-up, and outside every scrubber (they contain no scores or price adjectives).
fix: Relax the rule: allow 1 con + an honest 'data still filling in' when evidence is thin, and add meta-con patterns (limited information|no specific|lacks .* (data|reviews)|no .* noted) to a fail-closed drop in response_builder so data-availability statements never render as product cons.
verify_reason: The prompt line is confirmed verbatim at `extraction_service.py:982` ('NEVER return empty pros[] or cons[] arrays'), and meta-cons do pass every scrubber (has_score_internals at response_builder.py:1309 has no data-availability vocabulary; _leaks_price_adjective only fires on pended prices). But that is the whole verifiable content: the harm claim rests entirely on six recorded Supabase rows I could not open read-only here, and the inference - that a model under thin specs writes 'Limited detailed specs available' rather than the concrete qualitative attribute the same rule explicitly asks for - is an LLM-behaviour prediction, not a re-derived defect. It is also arguable copy policy rather than malfunction: 'Limited information on longevity' is honest evidence disclosure to the buyer, which is why no scrubber targets it. P3 (prompt/copy-design improvement) rather than P2.

title: clean_review_citations leaves 'Per domain: ' husks on trailing/interior citations and passes '[pcmag.com]'-form markers through untouched in persisted review text
evidence: Probe C on current code: 'Really rich smell that lasts all day [snippet_2]' → 'Really rich smell that lasts all day Per pcmag.com: ' (dangling attribution with trailing colon); 'Opens bright [3] then settles into florals' → 'Opens bright Per harrods.com: then settles into florals'; '[pcmag.com] The iPhone...' → unchanged (neither regex at :154/:164 matches a domain-bracket, a form the model emitted in 4 recorded production rows); an out-of-range [snippet_9] silently deletes the citation but keeps the claim, contradicting the prompt's cite-or-drop rule (extraction_service.py:914). These land in the persisted review_summary that history/share re-serve (and feed PO-verdict-text-03's praise corruption).
fix: Position-aware replacement: leading marker → 'Per {domain}: ' prefix; interior/trailing marker → strip and (optionally) append '({domain})'; add a domain-bracket branch \[([a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,})\]; drop the highlight when its only citation is out of range.
verify_reason: All four sub-claims reproduce on current code via the real clean_review_citations (`review_service.py:133-193`). Probe outputs: 'Really rich smell that lasts all day [snippet_2]' -> '... all day Per harrods.com: ' (dangling trailing attribution + colon); 'Opens bright [3] then settles into florals' -> 'Opens bright Per tomfordbeauty.com: then settles into florals'; '[pcmag.com] The iPhone 17 Pro Max is fast' -> unchanged (neither `:154` nor `:164` matches a domain-bracket); 'Great scent [snippet_9] worth it' -> 'Great scent worth it' (out-of-range citation silently deleted, claim retained, contradicting the cite-or-drop rule at extraction_service.py:914). `_attribute` (`:145-147`) is position-blind by construction. P3 is correct: review_summary is persisted/re-served but not FE-rendered, and `_strip_attribution` removes the 'Per domain:' husks before praise, so direct user-visible damage is bounded (the '[]' husk is separately filed as PO-03).

title: Verdict calibration coverage is uneven: 4/9 categories inject nothing, and no anti-pattern targets the dominant recorded failure mode (score-margin cited as the 'why')
evidence: Probe: build_exemplar_block returns '' for supplements/haircare/fashion/other (empty exemplars AND empty anti_patterns at verdict_exemplars.json:49-52, 78-81, 97-104) while electronics gets 825 chars — so 4 categories get zero Bahrain-buyer calibration. Meanwhile the dominant failure in the 15 recorded verdicts is winner_reason built from internal margins ('wins with a 24.4 point higher score', 'scores 73.8, outperforming... by 22.9 points' — 8 of 15 rows) — a failure mode no anti_pattern addresses (the 9 live anti-patterns cover prestige/climate/spec-sheet biases only), leaving only the prompt ban + regex scrub (whose gaps PO-verdict-text-04 shows). verify_reason: Independently re-derived by running the loader: build_exemplar_block returns 0 chars for supplements/haircare/fashion/other and 825 for electronics (grocery 311, makeup 523, skincare 299, fragrances 521) - those four categories carry empty exemplars AND empty anti_patterns in `data/verdict_exemplars.json` (parsed: every category has 0 exemplars; anti_patterns 3/1/0/2/1/0/2/0/0). The 9 live anti-patterns cover exactly three themes - global-prestige-over-GCC, climate-neutral-verdict, newer-spec-sheet - none about citing the size of the win. Injection site confirmed at `extraction_service.py:1915-1916`. One caveat that does not change the verdict: the 'dominant recorded failure mode' framing is weaker than stated, because `strip_score_internals` DOES catch the cited margin strings today (probe: 'wins with a 24.4 point higher score' and 'scores 73.8, outperforming ... by 22.9 points' both scrub to '' and fall back to the qualitative reason at response_builder.py:1379) - so the residual is a bland fallback, not a shipped margin claim.
